fullDescription: A loop with a condition inside runs one iteration per item, slowly. Filter array evaluates the whole array in one step. This pattern shows the basic and advanced modes, combined conditions, and how to read the result.
problemStatement: A flow takes minutes and thousands of action runs to find a handful of matching items, because it checks them one by one inside a loop.
whenToUse: Finding items in an array that match a condition
Filtering data from a connector that has no filter option
whenNotToUse: When the source connector can filter itself, such as a SharePoint filter query. Filter at the source first.
When every item needs an action, where a loop is still needed
stepByStepInstructions: Add the Data Operations action Filter array.
Set From to the array, such as the value output of Get items.
Enter the condition in basic mode, or switch to advanced mode for And, Or and functions.
Use the body of Filter array in later actions.
Remove the old loop and condition.
Compare run durations before and after.
commonMistakes: Passing the whole Get items body instead of its value array.
Comparing a number with a quoted value in basic mode, which makes it text.
Forgetting the leading @ in advanced mode.
Using dynamic content from the original Get items after the filter, which silently adds a new loop.
troubleshooting: If the result is empty, add a Compose with one item and check the property path. Choice and person columns need ?['Value'] or ?['Email'].
If you get a type error, convert with int(), float() or string() so both sides match.
If a new Apply to each appears by itself, you picked a field from the source action. Use item() or the Filter array output instead.
If dates do not compare correctly, make sure both are ISO strings, and use ticks() for exact comparisons.
seoTitle: Power Automate Filter array: multiple conditions and examples
seoDescription: Use Filter array in Power Automate instead of Apply to each with a Condition: basic and advanced mode, and/or expressions, contains, and reading the result.

faqs.question: How do I use multiple conditions in Filter array?
faqs.answer: Switch to advanced mode and combine them with @and(...) or @or(...).

faqs.question: How do I check whether Filter array found anything?
faqs.answer: Use length(body('Filter_array')) and compare it with zero.

faqs.question: Is Filter array faster than Apply to each?
faqs.answer: Yes. It is one action regardless of array size, while a loop runs every inner action once per item.

title: Reshape arrays with Select and remove duplicates with union
shortDescription: Turn an array of objects into the shape you need and get a distinct list, without loops or variables.
fullDescription: Select maps every item of an array to a new object or a simple value in one action. The union expression then removes duplicates. Together they replace the common pattern of a loop that appends to an array variable.
problemStatement: Flows build lists of email addresses or IDs with Apply to each and Append to array variable, which is slow, blocks concurrency and still leaves duplicates.
whenToUse: Building a recipient list from items
Getting distinct values of a column
Preparing rows for a table, CSV or card
whenNotToUse: When each item needs a connector call
Objects that differ in any property, which union treats as different
formulaOrCode:
1. Select: array of objects with new property names
   From : @{body('Get_items')?['value']}
   Map  :  Title    -> item()?['Title']
           Owner    -> item()?['AssignedTo']?['Email']
           Due      -> formatDateTime(item()?['DueDate'], 'yyyy-MM-dd')

2. Select: array of simple values (switch Map to text mode)
   From : @{body('Get_items')?['value']}
   Map  : @item()?['AssignedTo']?['Email']
   Result: ["a@contoso.com","b@contoso.com","a@contoso.com"]

3. Remove duplicates (Compose)
   union(body('Select_Emails'), body('Select_Emails'))
   Result: ["a@contoso.com","b@contoso.com"]

4. Use the distinct list
   To field of an email : join(outputs('Compose_Distinct'), ';')
   One email per owner  : Apply to each over outputs('Compose_Distinct'),
                          with a Filter array inside:
                          @equals(item()?['AssignedTo']?['Email'], items('Apply_to_each'))

Other set operations
   Items in both arrays : intersection(arrayA, arrayB)
   Remove empty values  : Filter array with @not(empty(item()))
stepByStepInstructions: Add a Select action and set From to the source array.
For objects, enter property names on the left and expressions on the right.
For a flat list, switch Map to text mode and enter a single expression.
Add a Compose with union of the Select output with itself to remove duplicates.
Use join to turn the list into text, or loop over the distinct list.
Delete the array variable and its loop.
commonMistakes: Using key-value mode when a flat list is needed, which produces objects instead of values.
Expecting union to remove duplicate objects that differ in one property.
Forgetting empty values, which become one blank entry in the distinct list.
Keeping the old loop alongside the new actions.
troubleshooting: If join fails, the Select produced objects. Switch Map to text mode.
If duplicates remain, they differ in case or spacing. Wrap the value in toLower(trim(...)) inside the Select.
If an email action fails on a blank address, filter out empty values before union.
If Select returns nulls, check the property path against one raw item in run history.
seoTitle: Power Automate Select action and union to remove duplicates
seoDescription: Use the Select action to reshape arrays and the union expression to remove duplicates in Power Automate, replacing loops and array variables.
primaryKeyword: Power Automate remove duplicates from array
secondaryKeywords: array of emails from Get items

faqs.question: How do I get distinct values in Power Automate?
faqs.answer: Build a flat array with Select in text mode, then use union(array, array). union returns each value once.

faqs.question: What does the Select action do?
faqs.answer: It transforms every item in an array into a new shape in one action, similar to a map function.

faqs.question: Why does union not remove my duplicate objects?
faqs.answer: Objects must match on every property to count as duplicates. Reduce them to the key value first.

title: Speed up Apply to each with concurrency, safely
shortDescription: Run loop iterations in parallel and avoid the variable bugs that parallel loops cause.
fullDescription: Apply to each runs one item at a time by default. Turning on concurrency can make a loop many times faster, but any Set variable inside it will then produce wrong results. This pattern shows the setting and the variable-free way to write the loop.
problemStatement: A loop over a few hundred items takes most of an hour, and when concurrency is switched on, values from one item turn up in another item's email.
whenToUse: Loops where each iteration calls a connector and does not depend on the others
Sending many emails, updating many items or creating many files
Flows that time out because of loop duration
whenNotToUse: Iterations that must run in order
Loops that build up a running total or a single string
Connectors with tight throttling limits
formulaOrCode:
Turn on concurrency
  Apply to each > Settings > Concurrency Control: On
  Degree of Parallelism: 20   (1 to 50; start at 20)

Unsafe inside a parallel loop
  Set variable varEmail = items('Apply_to_each')?['Owner']?['Email']
  Send an email To: variables('varEmail')
  // Variables are shared by all iterations, so another
  // iteration can overwrite varEmail before the email is sent.

Safe: use Compose, which is scoped to the iteration
  Compose_Email : items('Apply_to_each')?['Owner']?['Email']
  Send an email To: outputs('Compose_Email')

Safe: collect results without a variable
  After the loop, read the outputs of an action inside it:
    body('Update_item')          -> array of every iteration's result
  Or build the list first with Select and skip the loop.

Counting without a variable
  length(body('Filter_array'))

When order matters or throttling appears
  Concurrency Control: On, Degree of Parallelism: 1
stepByStepInstructions: Check that iterations are independent of each other.
Replace every Set variable inside the loop with a Compose, and refer to its output.
Replace Append to array variable with a Select before the loop, or read the loop action's outputs afterwards.
Open the loop's settings, turn on Concurrency Control and choose a degree of parallelism.
Run with test data and confirm each item received its own values.
Lower the parallelism if the connector returns 429 errors.
commonMistakes: Turning on concurrency while Set variable is still used inside the loop.
Setting parallelism to 50 against SharePoint or Outlook and being throttled.
Assuming results arrive in the original order.
Nesting parallel loops, which multiplies the load.
troubleshooting: If items receive each other's values, a variable is being set inside the loop. Use Compose.
If you see 429 Too Many Requests, reduce the degree of parallelism and let the built-in retry policy handle the rest.
If the loop is still slow, most time is in one connector action. Check whether a batch or filter option removes the need for the loop.
If an append variable has missing entries, parallel iterations overwrote each other. Build the array with Select.
seoTitle: Power Automate Apply to each concurrency and variables
seoDescription: Make Apply to each faster with concurrency control in Power Automate, and avoid wrong values by replacing variables inside the loop with Compose.
primaryKeyword: Power Automate Apply to each concurrency

faqs.question: Why are my variables wrong inside a parallel loop?
faqs.answer: Variables are global to the flow. With concurrency on, several iterations set the same variable at once. Use Compose inside the loop instead.

faqs.question: What degree of parallelism should I use?
faqs.answer: Start at 20 and reduce it if the connector throttles. The maximum is 50.

faqs.question: Does Apply to each run in order?
faqs.answer: Only when concurrency is off or set to 1.

title: Convert UTC to local time and format dates in Power Automate
shortDescription: Show the right local date and time in emails and messages, including daylight saving.
fullDescription: SharePoint, Dataverse and utcNow all return UTC. This pattern converts to a named time zone with convertFromUtc or convertTimeZone, formats the result, handles empty dates, and compares dates correctly.
problemStatement: Emails show times that are hours out, or a due date appears as the previous day, because the flow prints UTC values as they are.
whenToUse: Any date or time shown to a person
Scheduling logic that depends on local working hours
Comparing a date column with today
whenNotToUse: Storing or passing dates between systems. Keep those in UTC.
Adding fixed offsets with addHours, which breaks at daylight saving changes
stepByStepInstructions: Find the Windows time zone name for your users, such as GMT Standard Time or Eastern Standard Time.
Wrap each date shown to a person in convertFromUtc with that zone and a format string.
Guard optional dates with empty() so blank values do not fail the flow.
Compare dates as yyyy-MM-dd strings or with ticks().
Convert local times back to UTC before using them in filter queries.
Test with a time close to midnight to catch date shifts.
commonMistakes: Using addHours with a fixed offset, which is wrong for half the year.
Using mm for months. MM is months and mm is minutes.
Using hh without tt, which prints 02:00 for both 2 AM and 2 PM.
Passing an empty date to formatDateTime.
troubleshooting: "The datetime string must match ISO 8601 format" means the value is empty or not a date. Check it with empty() first, or build an ISO string.
"The time zone id is not valid" means the name is not a Windows time zone name. 'GMT Standard Time' is valid and 'BST' is not.
If a date-only column shows the previous day, it is midnight local time stored as UTC. Convert before formatting.
If the names of days and months are in the wrong language, pass a locale such as 'en-GB' as the last argument of formatDateTime.
seoTitle: Power Automate convert time zone and format date
seoDescription: Convert UTC to local time in Power Automate with convertFromUtc and convertTimeZone, format dates with formatDateTime, and handle empty dates.

faqs.question: How do I get the current local time in Power Automate?
faqs.answer: Use convertFromUtc(utcNow(), '<time zone name>', '<format>').

faqs.question: Does convertFromUtc handle daylight saving?
faqs.answer: Yes. Named time zones apply the correct offset for the date, which a fixed addHours cannot do.

faqs.question: Why does formatDateTime fail on some items?
faqs.answer: The date is empty on those items. Wrap the call in if(empty(...), '', formatDateTime(...)).

title: Handle null and empty values in Power Automate expressions
shortDescription: Stop flows failing on missing data with the question-mark operator, coalesce and empty.
fullDescription: Most flow failures on real data come from a value that is missing. This pattern gives the small set of expressions that make a flow tolerant of nulls: safe property access, default values, empty checks and type-safe conversion.
problemStatement: A flow works in testing and fails in production with "cannot be evaluated because property doesn't exist" or "the provided value is of type Null" when an optional field is left blank.
whenToUse: Optional columns such as manager, due date or comments
Data from forms, emails and HTTP responses
Before int(), formatDateTime() or string functions
whenNotToUse: Hiding a real data problem. If a value is required, fail clearly with Terminate instead of defaulting it.
Required trigger fields that can never be blank
stepByStepInstructions: Open a failed run and find the expression that received null.
Add ? before each property in the path so a missing level returns null.
Wrap the value in coalesce with a sensible default, or in an if(empty(...)) check.
Convert types only after the default has been applied.
For required values, add a Condition and Terminate with a clear message when the value is missing.
Re-run the failed run with the same data.
commonMistakes: Using coalesce for empty text. It only replaces null, so an empty string passes through.
Leaving out the question mark on the first level, as in triggerBody()['Manager'].
Comparing with the text 'null' instead of the null value.
Defaulting a required value silently, which hides bad data.
troubleshooting: "The template language expression cannot be evaluated because property 'X' doesn't exist" is fixed by adding ? before ['X'].
"The provided value is of type 'Null'" from a function means its input needs coalesce or an empty check.
If a Condition on null never matches, compare with the null expression, not with a blank text box.
If a default never applies, the value is an empty string rather than null. Use empty().
seoTitle: Power Automate null handling: coalesce, empty and ?
seoDescription: Handle null and empty values in Power Automate with the ? operator, coalesce, empty and safe conversions, with fixes for the common null errors.
secondaryKeywords: provided value is of type Null

faqs.question: What is the difference between coalesce and empty?
faqs.answer: coalesce returns the first value that is not null. empty returns true for null, an empty string, an empty array or an empty object.

faqs.question: What does the question mark do in an expression?
faqs.answer: It makes property access safe. If the property is missing, the expression returns null instead of failing.

faqs.question: How do I check for null in a Condition?
faqs.answer: Put the value on the left, choose is equal to, and enter null as an expression on the right.

title: Use Send an HTTP request to SharePoint for what the connector cannot do
shortDescription: Call the SharePoint REST API from a flow with the standard connector, with ready-to-use requests.
fullDescription: The action Send an HTTP request to SharePoint calls any SharePoint REST endpoint with the flow's connection and needs no premium licence. This pattern gives the headers and bodies for the tasks people most often need it for.
problemStatement: The SharePoint connector has no action for tasks such as updating an item without creating a new version, breaking permission inheritance or reading a list's column definitions.
whenToUse: Tasks with no dedicated SharePoint action
Updating only some fields without sending the rest
whenNotToUse: Anything a standard action already does. Standard actions are easier to maintain.
Calls to other Microsoft 365 services, which need Graph and a different connector
formulaOrCode:
All requests: Site Address = your site, plus these headers for JSON
  Accept       : application/json;odata=nometadata
  Content-Type : application/json;odata=nometadata

1. Update fields without adding a version
   Method : POST
   Uri    : _api/web/lists/getbytitle('Requests')/items(@{triggerBody()?['ID']})/validateUpdateListItem
   Body   :
   {
     "formValues": [
       { "FieldName": "Status", "FieldValue": "Processed" },
       { "FieldName": "ProcessedOn", "FieldValue": "@{utcNow()}" }
     ],
     "bNewDocumentUpdate": true
   }

2. Update a few fields (normal update)
   Method : POST
   Uri    : _api/web/lists/getbytitle('Requests')/items(@{triggerBody()?['ID']})
   Headers: IF-MATCH: *     X-HTTP-Method: MERGE
   Body   : { "Status": "Approved" }

3. Break inheritance on an item (keep nothing, clear existing)
   Method : POST
   Uri    : _api/web/lists/getbytitle('Requests')/items(@{triggerBody()?['ID']})/breakroleinheritance(copyRoleAssignments=false,clearSubscopes=true)

4. Grant a user Contribute on that item
   a. Get the user's ID
      Method : POST
      Uri    : _api/web/ensureuser
      Body   : { "logonName": "i:0#.f|membership|@{triggerBody()?['Author']?['Email']}" }
   b. Add the role (1073741827 = Contribute, 1073741826 = Read)
      Method : POST
      Uri    : _api/web/lists/getbytitle('Requests')/items(@{triggerBody()?['ID']})/roleassignments/addroleassignment(principalid=@{body('Ensure_user')?['Id']},roledefid=1073741827)

5. Read columns of a list
   Method : GET
   Uri    : _api/web/lists/getbytitle('Requests')/fields?$filter=Hidden eq false&$select=Title,InternalName,TypeAsString
stepByStepInstructions: Add the SharePoint action Send an HTTP request to SharePoint and choose the site.
Set the method and paste the Uri, starting with _api without a leading slash.
Add the Accept and Content-Type headers shown above.
Paste the body and replace list names and dynamic values.
Read results from the action's body, for example body('Send_an_HTTP_request_to_SharePoint')?['Id'].
Wrap the calls in a scope with error handling, since REST errors are less descriptive than connector errors.
commonMistakes: Using the list's display name after it has been renamed. Use getbytitle with the current title or the list GUID.
Leaving out IF-MATCH and X-HTTP-Method on a MERGE update.
Using display names for fields. REST needs internal names.
Breaking inheritance in a flow that then loses its own access to the item.
troubleshooting: 400 with "Invalid JSON" usually means the Content-Type header is missing or the body has a trailing comma.
403 means the flow's connection account lacks permission, for example Manage Permissions when breaking inheritance.
404 means the list title or item ID in the Uri is wrong.
If validateUpdateListItem returns 200 but nothing changes, read the response body. Each field reports its own error message there.
seoTitle: Send an HTTP request to SharePoint: Power Automate examples
seoDescription: Power Automate examples for Send an HTTP request to SharePoint: update without a new version, MERGE updates, break inheritance, grant permissions, read fields.
primaryKeyword: Send an HTTP request to SharePoint

faqs.question: Is Send an HTTP request to SharePoint a premium action?
faqs.answer: No. It is part of the standard SharePoint connector and uses the same connection as the other SharePoint actions.

faqs.question: How do I update an item without creating a new version?
faqs.answer: Use validateUpdateListItem with bNewDocumentUpdate set to true. The update still fires item-modified triggers, so add a trigger condition to stop the flow re-running on its own change.

faqs.question: Which role definition IDs are standard?
faqs.answer: 1073741826 is Read, 1073741827 is Contribute, 1073741828 is Design, 1073741830 is Edit and 1073741829 is Full Control.

title: Return values from a flow to Power Apps
shortDescription: Call a flow from a button, wait for it, and use what it sends back.
fullDescription: The Power Apps (V2) trigger with the action Respond to a Power App or flow turns a flow into a function the app can call. This pattern covers inputs, outputs, error reporting and the formula that handles success and failure.
problemStatement: An app starts a flow and immediately tells the user it worked, with no idea whether the flow succeeded or what it produced.
whenToUse: The app needs an ID, a link or a status back from the flow
Operations the app cannot do itself, such as creating files or calling an API
Showing a real success or failure message
whenNotToUse: Long-running work. The app waits up to two minutes for a response.
Fire-and-forget notifications, where no response is needed
stepByStepInstructions: Create the flow with the Power Apps (V2) trigger and add typed inputs.
Put the work in a scope so success and failure can be handled separately.
Add one Respond action for success and one configured to run after failure, with the same output names and types.
Add the flow to the app and call it with Run, storing the result in a variable.
Check the status output and show the message.
Disable the button while the call is in progress.
commonMistakes: Responding with different output names in the success and failure branches, which the app cannot handle.
Changing the flow's inputs or outputs and not removing and re-adding it in the app.
Putting long work before the Respond action, so the app times out.
Ignoring the result and showing a success message unconditionally.
troubleshooting: If the app shows an error about an invalid response, the two Respond actions return different schemas. Make them identical.
If new inputs do not appear in the app, remove the flow from the app and add it again.
If the app times out, respond first and continue the long work after the Respond action.
If the output name looks different in the app, note that Power Apps lowercases output names, as in locResult.itemid.
seoTitle: Power Automate: respond to a Power App with return values
seoDescription: Return values from a Power Automate flow to Power Apps using the Power Apps (V2) trigger and Respond to a Power App or flow, with error handling.
primaryKeyword: Respond to a Power App or flow
secondaryKeywords: return value from flow to Power Apps

faqs.question: How long will Power Apps wait for a flow?
faqs.answer: About two minutes. Respond before then and continue any long-running work afterwards.

faqs.question: Can a flow return a table to Power Apps?
faqs.answer: Not directly with this action. Return the array as JSON text and convert it in the app with ParseJSON.

faqs.question: Why did my app break after I edited the flow?
faqs.answer: The app caches the flow's inputs and outputs. Remove the flow from the app and add it again after changing them.

title: Convert Excel date serial numbers in Power Automate
shortDescription: Turn values like 46346 from List rows present in a table into real dates.
fullDescription: Excel stores dates as the number of days since 30 December 1899. The Excel connector returns that number unless told otherwise. This pattern shows the connector setting that avoids the problem and the expression that fixes it when you cannot.
problemStatement: A flow reading an Excel table writes 46346 into a SharePoint date column, or fails with a message that the value is not a valid date.
whenToUse: Importing Excel rows into SharePoint or Dataverse
Emails that show dates from a workbook
Any flow using List rows present in a table
whenNotToUse: Columns formatted as text in Excel, which already arrive as text
CSV files, which have no serial numbers
stepByStepInstructions: Open the List rows present in a table action and show the advanced options.
Set DateTime Format to ISO 8601 and run the flow.
If a column still returns a number, wrap it in the addDays expression.
Add the empty check for optional date cells.
Write the result to the date column in SharePoint or Dataverse.
Check a known date in the output to confirm it is not a day out.
commonMistakes: Using 1900-01-01 as the base date, which gives a result two days late.
Passing a decimal serial number to int() directly, which fails. Convert with float first.
Leaving empty cells unguarded.
Relying on the Excel connector's Filter Query for date comparisons instead of Filter array.
troubleshooting: If the date is two days out, the base date is wrong. Use 1899-12-30.
"The template language function 'int' was invoked with a parameter that is not valid" means the cell is empty or has a decimal. Add the empty check and convert through float.
If times are wrong by a few hours, the workbook stores local time. Treat the result as local and convert to UTC if the target needs it.
If only 256 rows arrive, turn on pagination in the action's settings.
seoTitle: Power Automate Excel date shows as number: how to convert
seoDescription: Fix Excel dates arriving as serial numbers in Power Automate: set DateTime Format to ISO 8601, or convert with addDays from 1899-12-30.
secondaryKeywords: List rows present in a table date format

faqs.question: Why does Excel return a number instead of a date?
faqs.answer: Excel stores dates as a count of days since 30 December 1899. The connector returns that raw value unless DateTime Format is set to ISO 8601.

faqs.question: Why 1899-12-30 and not 1900-01-01?
faqs.answer: Excel counts 1 January 1900 as day 1 and also includes a non-existent 29 February 1900, so the effective zero point is 30 December 1899.

faqs.question: Why do I only get 256 rows from Excel?
faqs.answer: That is the default page size. Turn on pagination in the action's settings and set a higher threshold.

title: Upsert Dataverse rows with an alternate key in Power Automate
shortDescription: Create or update a Dataverse row in one action by addressing it with an alternate key instead of looking up its GUID first.
fullDescription: Data arriving from another system knows its own identifier, not the Dataverse GUID. An alternate key lets a flow address a row by that identifier. A single update call then creates the row if it is missing and updates it if it exists, with no List rows step and no condition.
problemStatement: Every import flow does List rows, checks whether anything came back, then branches into Add a new row or Update a row. It is slow, doubles the API calls and creates duplicates when two runs overlap.
whenToUse: Loading rows from another system that has its own unique identifier
Flows that may receive the same record more than once
Setting lookups to rows you know only by an external code
whenNotToUse: Tables with no stable natural identifier
Keys built on columns users edit freely, since a changed value creates a second row
formulaOrCode:
1. Define the key (once)
   Table > Keys > New key
     Name: cnt_ExternalIdKey        Columns: cnt_ExternalId
   Wait for the key's status to become Active (an index is built in the background).
   Key columns can be text, whole number, decimal, lookup, choice or date. Up to 16 columns per key.

2. Upsert with the Dataverse connector
   Action: Update a row      (this action upserts when the row ID does not exist)
     Table name: Customers
     Row ID:     cnt_externalid='@{items('Apply_to_each')?['CustomerCode']}'
     Name:       @{items('Apply_to_each')?['Name']}
     Email:      @{items('Apply_to_each')?['Email']}
   Composite key Row ID:   cnt_region='EU',cnt_code='@{variables('varCode')}'
   Text values need single quotes. Numbers do not. Encode quotes inside values by doubling them.

3. Same call through the Web API (Invoke an HTTP request, or the Perform an unbound action pattern)
   PATCH /api/data/v9.2/cnt_customers(cnt_externalid='C-1042')
   { "cnt_name": "Contoso", "emailaddress1": "info@contoso.com" }
   Header  If-Match: *          update only, never create
   Header  If-None-Match: *     create only, never update

4. Set a lookup by the related row's alternate key
   "cnt_Account@odata.bind": "/accounts(accountnumber='A-2001')"
   In the connector's lookup field:  accounts(accountnumber='A-2001')

5. Read a row by key
   Get a row by ID > Row ID: cnt_externalid='C-1042'
stepByStepInstructions: Choose the column or columns that uniquely identify a row outside Dataverse.
Create a key on the table and wait until it is Active.
In the flow, use Update a row with the key expression as the Row ID.
Map the remaining columns as usual.
Use the same key syntax to set lookups to related rows.
Run the flow twice with the same data and confirm no duplicate appears.
commonMistakes: Using List rows and a Condition to decide between create and update.
Forgetting single quotes around text key values.
Creating a key on a column that already contains duplicate values, so the key never activates.
Leaving the key column out of the solution.
troubleshooting: If the action fails with 'Resource not found for the segment', check the key expression uses the column's logical name in lower case.
If the key stays in Failed status, remove duplicate or oversized values and reactivate it.
If a duplicate row appears, the flow wrote a different value into the key column, such as trailing spaces. Trim it first.
If a value contains a single quote, double it with replace(value, '''', '''''').
seoTitle: Upsert Dataverse rows with an alternate key in Power Automate
seoDescription: Create or update a Dataverse row in one action by addressing it with an alternate key instead of looking up its GUID first.
primaryKeyword: Dataverse upsert alternate key Power Automate

faqs.question: How do I upsert a row in Dataverse from Power Automate?
faqs.answer: Create an alternate key on the table, then use Update a row with the key expression, such as cnt_externalid='C-1042', as the Row ID. The row is created when it does not exist.

faqs.question: What is an alternate key in Dataverse?
faqs.answer: A column or set of columns declared unique on a table, so rows can be addressed by those values instead of the GUID.

faqs.question: Can I stop an upsert from creating rows?
faqs.answer: Yes, through the Web API. Send the PATCH with the header If-Match: * and it will only update existing rows.

title: Generate request numbers with a Dataverse autonumber column
shortDescription: Give every row a readable reference such as REQ-001042 with an autonumber column, including date and random segments, and reset the seed after a migration.
fullDescription: People quote reference numbers, not GUIDs. An autonumber column produces one on the server when a row is created, so numbers are unique whichever app, flow or import created the row. The format can combine text, a sequence, the date and random characters.
problemStatement: Reference numbers are built in the app with CountRows plus one, so two users get the same number, and rows created by flows or imports have none.
whenToUse: Requests, cases, orders or any row users refer to by number
Rows created from several apps, flows or imports
As the table's primary name column, so lookups show the number
whenNotToUse: Numbers that must have no gaps, since deleted or failed creates leave gaps
Numbering that restarts per parent row or per year, which needs custom logic
formulaOrCode:
Create the column
  Table > Columns > New column
    Data type: Autonumber (under Text)
    Autonumber type: String prefixed number | Date prefixed number | Custom
    Prefix: REQ      Minimum number of digits: 6      Seed value: 1000
  Preview: REQ-001000

Custom formats
  REQ-{SEQNUM:6}                         REQ-001000
  {DATETIMEUTC:yyyy}-{SEQNUM:5}          2026-01000
  CASE-{DATETIMEUTC:yyMM}-{SEQNUM:4}     CASE-2603-1000
  WO-{RANDSTRING:4}-{SEQNUM:6}           WO-K7QX-001000
  SEQNUM length is a minimum: numbers keep growing past it. RANDSTRING is 1 to 6 characters.
  The date segment is UTC and does not restart the sequence.

Make it the primary name
  When creating the table: Primary column > Advanced options > data type Autonumber is not offered there, so
  either convert the existing primary column (Edit column > Data type > Autonumber) or keep a separate
  autonumber column and show it first in views and the form header.

Use it in a canvas app
  Do not send a value. Dataverse fills it on create.
  Set(gblNew, Patch('Service Requests', Defaults('Service Requests'), { Subject: txtSubject.Text }));
  Notify("Created " & gblNew.'Request Number', NotificationType.Success)

Change the next number (after importing old rows)
  Maker portal: Edit column > Seed value applies only before rows exist.
  Later, call the SetAutoNumberSeed action:
  POST /api/data/v9.2/SetAutoNumberSeed
  { "EntityName": "cnt_servicerequest", "AttributeName": "cnt_requestnumber", "Value": 250000 }
  XrmToolBox "Auto Number Manager" does the same with a form.

Imports
  If the import file supplies a value for the column, that value is kept and the sequence is not advanced.
  Set the seed above the highest imported number afterwards.
stepByStepInstructions: Add an autonumber column to the table, or convert the primary column.
Choose the format, digits and starting seed.
Add the column to the main form as read-only and to the key views.
Remove any app or flow logic that builds numbers by hand.
Create a test row from the app and from a flow and compare the numbers.
After a data migration, set the seed above the highest imported value.
commonMistakes: Calculating the number in the app with a row count.
Expecting the sequence to restart each year because the format includes the year.
Sending a blank string for the column from a flow, which stores blank on some paths. Leave the field out instead.
Seeding below existing values after an import, which causes duplicate key errors when a key is on the column.
troubleshooting: If numbers are blank on new rows, the column was populated by the create request. Remove it from the Patch or flow action.
If two environments produce the same numbers, that is expected. Use a different prefix per environment if rows are ever merged.
If the seed setting has no effect, rows already exist. Use SetAutoNumberSeed.
If users need to search by number, add the column to the table's Quick Find view.
seoTitle: Generate request numbers with a Dataverse autonumber column
seoDescription: Give every row a readable reference such as REQ-001042 with an autonumber column, including date and random segments, and reset the seed after a migration.

faqs.question: How do I create an auto-incrementing number in Dataverse?
faqs.answer: Add a column with the Autonumber data type and choose a format such as REQ-{SEQNUM:6}. Dataverse assigns the next number when each row is created.

faqs.question: Can I reset a Dataverse autonumber sequence?
faqs.answer: Yes. Call the SetAutoNumberSeed action through the Web API or a tool such as Auto Number Manager to set the next value.

faqs.question: Will autonumber values have gaps?
faqs.answer: They can. A number is consumed even if the create later fails or the row is deleted, so do not rely on an unbroken sequence.

title: Add calculated values with Dataverse formula columns
shortDescription: Use Power Fx formula columns for values such as totals, ages and flags that every app, view and flow should see the same way.
fullDescription: A formula column is defined once on the table with Power Fx and calculated by Dataverse whenever it is read. Apps, views, flows and reports all get the same answer without repeating the logic. They are the current replacement for classic calculated columns in most cases.
problemStatement: The same calculation, such as days open or line total, is rewritten in the canvas app, the flow and the Power BI report, and the three versions drift apart.
whenToUse: Values derived from other columns on the same row
Values pulled from a parent row through a lookup
Flags and labels used in views and filters
whenNotToUse: Totals over child rows, which need a rollup column or a flow
Values that must be stored and indexed for heavy filtering on very large tables
formulaOrCode:
Create: Table > Columns > New column > Data type: Formula (fx)

Arithmetic
  Line total              cnt_Quantity * cnt_UnitPrice
  With discount           cnt_Quantity * cnt_UnitPrice * (1 - cnt_DiscountPercent / 100)
  Rounded                 Round(cnt_Amount * 0.2, 2)

Dates
  Days open               DateDiff('Created On', UTCNow(), TimeUnit.Days)
  Due date                DateAdd('Created On', 14, TimeUnit.Days)
  Is overdue              cnt_DueDate < UTCToday() && cnt_Status <> 'Status (Service Requests)'.Closed

Text
  Display name            cnt_FirstName & " " & cnt_LastName
  Short reference         Left(cnt_RequestNumber, 8)
  Clean code              Upper(Trim(cnt_Code))

Conditions
  Priority band           If(cnt_Amount >= 10000, "High", cnt_Amount >= 1000, "Medium", "Low")
  Switch on a choice      Switch(cnt_Priority, 'Priority'.High, 1, 'Priority'.Normal, 2, 3)

Values from a parent row (through a lookup, one or more levels)
  Account city            cnt_Account.'Address 1: City'
  Owner manager name      cnt_Account.'Primary Contact'.'Full Name'

Blank handling
  Safe division           If(IsBlank(cnt_Total) || cnt_Total = 0, 0, cnt_Done / cnt_Total)
  Fallback text           Coalesce(cnt_PreferredName, cnt_FirstName)

Result types: text, decimal, whole number, yes/no, date and time, choice (in newer releases).
Formula columns are read-only. They can be shown on forms and in views, sorted and filtered.
Use UTCNow() and UTCToday() for values everyone should agree on. Now() and Today() are user-local and limit
where the column can be used.
stepByStepInstructions: Open the table and add a column with the Formula data type.
Write the Power Fx expression using the table's column display names.
Save and check the inferred result type.
Add the column to a view and a form and confirm the values.
Replace the duplicate logic in apps, flows and reports with the new column.
Add the column to your solution.
commonMistakes: Using a formula column for a sum over child rows.
Referring to columns by a name that has since changed, which breaks the formula.
Using Today() where the result must be the same for users in different time zones.
Expecting to write to the column from an app or flow.
troubleshooting: If the editor rejects a function, it is not supported in formula columns. Check the supported list and simplify.
If the column cannot be used in a view filter, the formula uses a user-local function such as Now().
If the value looks stale in a report, the report cached it. Formula columns are calculated on read.
If saving fails after a referenced column was deleted, edit the formula to remove the reference.
seoTitle: Add calculated values with Dataverse formula columns
seoDescription: Use Power Fx formula columns for values such as totals, ages and flags that every app, view and flow should see the same way.

faqs.question: What is a formula column in Dataverse?
faqs.answer: A read-only column whose value is defined with a Power Fx expression and calculated by Dataverse when the row is read.

faqs.question: What is the difference between formula columns and calculated columns?
faqs.answer: Formula columns use Power Fx and support more functions. Calculated columns use the older editor. Microsoft recommends formula columns for new work.

faqs.question: Can a formula column sum related rows?
faqs.answer: No. Use a rollup column for aggregates over child rows.

title: Total child rows with Dataverse rollup columns
shortDescription: Show a count, sum, minimum, maximum or average of related rows on the parent with a rollup column, and refresh it on demand when hourly is not enough.
fullDescription: A rollup column stores an aggregate of child rows on the parent, such as the total of an order's lines or the number of open tasks on a project. Dataverse recalculates it on a schedule, and a flow or button can force a refresh for one row when the value must be current.
problemStatement: The parent form needs a total, so the app sums child rows on every load, which is slow and not delegable, or a flow maintains a number that drifts out of step.
whenToUse: Counts and totals of child rows shown on the parent
Totals needed in views, charts and filters
Aggregates over a hierarchy of rows
whenNotToUse: Values that must be exact the instant a child row changes
Aggregates that depend on other rollup or complex formula columns
formulaOrCode:
Create: Parent table > Columns > New column
  Data type: Whole number, Decimal, Currency or Date and time      Behavior: Rollup
  Editor:
    Source entity      Order (the parent)        Use hierarchy: No
    Related entity     Order Lines (Order)       Filters:  Status equals Active
    Aggregation        SUM of Line Amount
  Other aggregations: COUNT, MIN, MAX, AVG

Examples
  Open task count          COUNT of Tasks           filter: Status Reason does not equal Completed
  Order total              SUM of Order Lines.Line Amount
  Latest activity date     MAX of Activities.Actual End
  Earliest due date        MIN of Tasks.Due Date    filter: Status equals Active

What Dataverse adds
  cnt_ordertotal           the value
  cnt_ordertotal_date      when it was last calculated
  cnt_ordertotal_state     0 not calculated, 1 calculated, other values are error states

Refresh timing
  First calculation: a Mass Calculate job, 12 hours after the column is created (can be brought forward in
  Settings > System jobs).
  Then: a recurring job, hourly at most. Model-driven forms show a refresh icon beside the field.

Force a refresh for one row from a flow
  Dataverse > Perform a bound action is not available for this function, so call the Web API:
  GET /api/data/v9.2/CalculateRollupField(Target=@t,FieldName=@f)
      ?@t={'@odata.id':'cnt_orders(<order guid>)'}&@f='cnt_ordertotal'
  With the HTTP with Microsoft Entra ID connector ("Invoke an HTTP request"), base URL = the environment URL.
  Trigger it from: when an Order Line is added, modified or deleted.

Canvas app
  Read the stored value:  ThisItem.'Order Total'      (delegable, sortable)
  After saving a line, call a flow that runs CalculateRollupField, then Refresh(Orders).

Limits
  Up to 200 rollup columns per environment and 50 per table (raised from earlier limits; check current docs).
  A rollup cannot reference another rollup, or a formula column that uses a rollup.
  Filters are fixed conditions. They cannot compare with the current user.
stepByStepInstructions: Add a column on the parent table with Rollup behavior.
Choose the related table, filter and aggregation.
Add the column to the parent form and views.
Bring forward the first Mass Calculate job if you need values immediately.
Add a flow that calls CalculateRollupField when child rows change, if hourly is too slow.
Read the stored value in canvas apps instead of summing child rows.
commonMistakes: Expecting the value to change the moment a child row is saved.
Summing child rows in a gallery when a rollup would do.
Filtering the rollup on another rollup column.
Forgetting that currency rollups use the base currency.
troubleshooting: If the value is blank on all rows, the first Mass Calculate job has not run. Start it from System jobs.
If one row is wrong, refresh it from the form or call CalculateRollupField.
If the state column shows an error, a referenced column was changed or removed. Reopen and save the rollup definition.
If the refresh flow fails with 404, check the entity set name and that the GUID has no braces.
seoTitle: Total child rows with Dataverse rollup columns
seoDescription: Show a count, sum, minimum, maximum or average of related rows on the parent with a rollup column, and refresh it on demand when hourly is not enough.

faqs.question: How often do Dataverse rollup columns update?
faqs.answer: A system job recalculates them about hourly. Users can refresh one row from a model-driven form, and a flow can call CalculateRollupField.

faqs.question: Can I use a rollup column in a canvas app?
faqs.answer: Yes. It is a normal stored column, so it can be shown, sorted and filtered with delegation.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a rollup column and a formula column?
faqs.answer: A rollup aggregates related child rows and is stored. A formula column calculates from the row itself or its parents and is worked out when read.

title: Filter Dataverse rows in Power Automate with OData
shortDescription: Write the Filter rows query for List rows: text, numbers, dates, choices, lookups, null checks and combined conditions, with the right column names.
fullDescription: The List rows action takes an OData filter. Getting it right means using logical column names, the special name for lookups, and the right literal format for each data type. This reference covers the cases that come up in almost every Dataverse flow.
problemStatement: A flow lists every row in the table and uses a Condition inside Apply to each to find the few it needs, because the Filter rows syntax kept returning errors.
whenToUse: Any List rows action that should return a subset
Scheduled flows that process rows by status or date
Looking up a row by a business identifier
whenNotToUse: Aggregates and complex joins, which are easier in FetchXML
Row counts above what a single flow run should process without pagination planning
formulaOrCode:
Use logical names (lower case, with prefix). Find them in the column's details: cnt_duedate.

Text
  cnt_name eq 'Contoso'
  contains(cnt_name, 'cont')          startswith(cnt_name, 'Con')          endswith(emailaddress1, '@contoso.com')
  cnt_name eq '@{triggerOutputs()?['body/cnt_name']}'
  Single quote inside a value: double it       cnt_name eq 'O''Brien'

Numbers and currency
  cnt_amount gt 1000          cnt_quantity le 10          cnt_amount ge 100 and cnt_amount lt 500

Yes/No
  cnt_isurgent eq true

Choice (use the numeric value)
  cnt_priority eq 100000002
  statecode eq 0                      Active rows
  statuscode eq 1
  Multi-select choice:  Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.ContainValues(PropertyName='cnt_systems',PropertyValues=['100000001'])

Dates
  cnt_duedate lt @{utcNow()}                          (no quotes around date values)
  cnt_duedate ge @{startOfDay(utcNow())}
  createdon ge @{addDays(utcNow(), -7)}
  Date-only column: cnt_startdate eq @{formatDateTime(utcNow(), 'yyyy-MM-dd')}
  Built-in functions:
  Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.Today(PropertyName='cnt_duedate')
  Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.LastXDays(PropertyName='createdon',PropertyValue=7)
  Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.ThisMonth(PropertyName='createdon')

Lookup (use _name_value and a GUID without quotes)
  _cnt_account_value eq 0f8fad5b-d9cb-469f-a165-70867728950e
  _ownerid_value eq @{triggerOutputs()?['body/_ownerid_value']}
  _cnt_account_value eq null                         no account set

Filter on a parent row's column
  cnt_Account/name eq 'Contoso'                      (navigation property, case sensitive, then the column)

Null checks
  cnt_closedon eq null          cnt_closedon ne null

Combine
  statecode eq 0 and (cnt_priority eq 100000002 or cnt_isurgent eq true)
  not contains(cnt_name, 'test')

Other fields on the action
  Select columns:  cnt_name,cnt_duedate,_cnt_account_value         fewer columns, faster
  Sort by:         cnt_duedate asc, createdon desc
  Row count:       1 when you expect one row
  Expand query:    cnt_Account($select=name,accountnumber)
stepByStepInstructions: Find the logical names of the columns you need.
Write the filter with the right literal format for each type.
Add Select columns to return only what the flow uses.
Set Row count when only the first match is needed.
Run the flow and check the number of rows returned in the action's output.
Turn on pagination in the action settings when more than 5,000 rows are expected.
commonMistakes: Using display names or schema names with capital letters.
Putting quotes around GUIDs, numbers or dates.
Filtering a lookup by its column name without _value.
Filtering inside Apply to each instead of in the query.
troubleshooting: If the error says a property could not be found, the logical name is wrong or a lookup is missing its _value form.
If a choice filter returns nothing, compare with the numeric value, not the label.
If the parent-column filter fails, use the navigation property name exactly as shown in the table's relationship, including capitals.
If only 5,000 rows come back, enable Pagination and set a threshold.
seoTitle: Filter Dataverse rows in Power Automate with OData
seoDescription: Write the Filter rows query for List rows: text, numbers, dates, choices, lookups, null checks and combined conditions, with the right column names.

faqs.question: How do I filter by a lookup column in List rows?
faqs.answer: Use the form _columnname_value eq followed by the GUID with no quotes, for example _cnt_account_value eq 0f8fad5b-d9cb-469f-a165-70867728950e.

faqs.question: How do I filter Dataverse rows by a choice value?
faqs.answer: Compare the column with the choice's numeric value, such as cnt_priority eq 100000002.

faqs.question: Why does my Dataverse filter say the property does not exist?
faqs.answer: The filter needs the column's logical name in lower case. Lookups need the _name_value form.

title: Get related Dataverse rows in one call with Expand query
shortDescription: Return parent columns and child rows with the same List rows or Get a row action by using Expand query, instead of a second lookup inside a loop.
fullDescription: Expand query follows a relationship and brings back columns from the related table in the same response. One call can return a request with its account's name, or an order with all its lines. It removes the Get a row inside Apply to each that makes many Dataverse flows slow.
problemStatement: A flow lists 200 requests, then calls Get a row by ID for each one to fetch the account name. It makes 201 calls and takes minutes.
whenToUse: Emails and documents that need parent details
Processing a parent with its child rows
whenNotToUse: Child collections with thousands of rows per parent, where a separate filtered List rows pages better
Relationships you cannot name, such as ad hoc matches on non-key columns
formulaOrCode:
Many-to-one (child to parent): use the lookup's navigation property name
  List rows > Table: Service Requests
    Select columns:  cnt_name,cnt_duedate
    Expand query:    cnt_Account($select=name,accountnumber,address1_city)
  Read in the loop:
    items('Apply_to_each')?['cnt_Account']?['name']
    items('Apply_to_each')?['cnt_Account/address1_city']       (also works for single-valued expansions)

  Several parents at once:
    cnt_Account($select=name),ownerid($select=fullname,internalemailaddress),createdby($select=fullname)
  Owner is polymorphic. Use the typed property for users:
    owninguser($select=fullname,internalemailaddress)

One-to-many (parent to children): use the relationship's collection name
  Get a row by ID > Table: Orders
    Expand query:    cnt_Order_cnt_OrderLine($select=cnt_name,cnt_quantity,cnt_lineamount;$filter=statecode eq 0;$orderby=cnt_name asc)
  Options inside the brackets are separated by semicolons.
  Read the children:
    outputs('Get_order')?['body/cnt_Order_cnt_OrderLine']        an array for Select, Create HTML table or Apply to each

Nested (parent of the parent)
  cnt_Account($select=name;$expand=primarycontactid($select=fullname,emailaddress1))

Finding the names
  Maker portal > Table > Relationships: the "Relationship name" is the collection name for one-to-many.
  For lookups, the navigation property is usually the lookup's schema name (case sensitive): cnt_Account.
  Or read them from <environment>/api/data/v9.2/$metadata.

Filtering the parent list on a child or parent value
  Filter rows: cnt_Account/name eq 'Contoso'
  Filter rows: cnt_Order_cnt_OrderLine/any(l: l/cnt_lineamount gt 1000)

Limits
  Up to 15 expands per query. Expanded collections return up to 5,000 rows each and are not paged.
  Expanding collections in List rows is slower. Prefer it on Get a row, or filter the parent list tightly.
stepByStepInstructions: Find the navigation property name for the lookup or relationship.
Add it to Expand query with a $select of the columns you need.
For child collections, add $filter and $orderby inside the brackets.
Reference the expanded values in later actions.
Remove the Get a row actions that the expand replaced.
Compare run duration before and after.
commonMistakes: Using the logical name in lower case where the navigation property has capitals.
Separating options inside the brackets with commas or ampersands instead of semicolons.
Expanding without $select, returning every column of the related row.
Expecting expanded child rows to page beyond 5,000.
troubleshooting: If the error says the property could not be found, check the exact case of the navigation property in $metadata.
If the expanded value is null, the lookup is empty on that row. Wrap reads in coalesce().
If owner details are missing, expand owninguser or owningteam instead of ownerid.
If the flow is slower after expanding children in List rows, move the expand to a Get a row or query the child table directly.
seoTitle: Get related Dataverse rows in one call with Expand query
seoDescription: Return parent columns and child rows with the same List rows or Get a row action by using Expand query, instead of a second lookup inside a loop.

faqs.question: What does Expand query do in the Dataverse connector?
faqs.answer: It returns columns from related rows, parents or children, in the same response as the main row.

faqs.question: How do I get the name from a lookup column in Power Automate?
faqs.answer: Expand the lookup's navigation property with $select=name, or read the lookup's formatted value: body/_cnt_account_value@OData.Community.Display.V1.FormattedValue.

faqs.question: Can I filter the expanded child rows?
faqs.answer: Yes. Add $filter inside the brackets, separated from $select by a semicolon.

title: Set and clear Dataverse lookup columns in Power Automate
shortDescription: Fill a lookup in Add a new row or Update a row with the entity set name and GUID, handle customer and owner lookups, and clear a lookup with Unrelate rows.
fullDescription: Lookup fields in the Dataverse connector do not take a name or a bare GUID. They take a reference to the related row in the form entitysetname(guid). Polymorphic lookups such as Customer and Owner show one field per target table. Clearing a lookup needs a different action altogether.
problemStatement: The flow fails with 'Resource not found for the segment' or 'URL was not parsed due to an ODataUnrecognizedPathException' whenever it tries to set a lookup.
whenToUse: Creating or updating rows that reference other rows
Removing a relationship without deleting either row
whenNotToUse: Many-to-many relationships, which use Relate rows and Unrelate rows only
Setting lookups to rows the connection's user cannot read
formulaOrCode:
Format: <entity set name>(<guid>)

  Account lookup          accounts(0f8fad5b-d9cb-469f-a165-70867728950e)
  Custom table lookup     cnt_projects(@{outputs('Get_project')?['body/cnt_projectid']})
  From a previous List rows item:
                          accounts(@{items('Apply_to_each')?['accountid']})
  From another row's lookup:
                          accounts(@{triggerOutputs()?['body/_cnt_account_value']})

  The entity set name is the plural logical name: account > accounts, contact > contacts,
  cnt_project > cnt_projects, cnt_category > cnt_categories. Check it under Table > Properties > Advanced
  options > "Logical collection name", or copy it from another action's @odata.id output.
  No quotes, no braces, no leading slash is needed (a leading slash also works).

Customer lookup (Account or Contact): the action shows two fields. Fill exactly one.
  Customer (Accounts)     accounts(<guid>)
  Customer (Contacts)     contacts(<guid>)

Owner
  Owner (Users)           systemusers(<user guid>)
  Owner (Teams)           teams(<team guid>)
  Find the user row:  List rows > Users > Filter rows: internalemailaddress eq '@{variables('varEmail')}'
                      > first(outputs('List_users')?['body/value'])?['systemuserid']

By alternate key instead of GUID
  accounts(accountnumber='A-2001')

Lookup may be empty: only set it when there is a value
  if(empty(triggerOutputs()?['body/_cnt_account_value']), null,
     concat('accounts(', triggerOutputs()?['body/_cnt_account_value'], ')'))

Clear a lookup
  Update a row cannot blank a lookup by leaving the field empty (empty means "do not change").
  Use: Unrelate rows
    Table name:    the table that holds the lookup (Service Requests)
    Row ID:        the row to change
    Relationship:  the lookup relationship (Account)
    Unrelate with: the full URL of the related row
                   @{outputs('Get_request')?['body/cnt_Account@odata.id']}   or
                   https://<env>.crm.dynamics.com/api/data/v9.2/accounts(<guid>)

In raw Web API calls the same thing is written as
  "cnt_Account@odata.bind": "/accounts(<guid>)"          (navigation property name, case sensitive)
stepByStepInstructions: Find the related table's entity set name.
Get the related row's GUID from the trigger, a Get a row or a List rows action.
Enter entitysetname(guid) in the lookup field.
For Customer and Owner, fill only the field for the right target table.
Wrap the value in an if() expression when the source may be empty.
Use Unrelate rows when the lookup has to be cleared.
commonMistakes: Typing the related row's name into the lookup field.
Using the singular table name or the display name.
Filling both the Accounts and Contacts fields of a customer lookup.
Leaving the field blank and expecting the lookup to be cleared.
troubleshooting: If you see 'Resource not found for the segment', the entity set name is wrong. Check the logical collection name.
If the action reports a bad GUID, the dynamic value is empty or includes text. Check the previous action's output.
If the lookup saves but shows a different row, the GUID came from the wrong column, such as the row's own ID.
If Unrelate rows fails, pass the full OData URL of the related row, not just its GUID.
seoTitle: Set and clear Dataverse lookup columns in Power Automate
seoDescription: Fill a lookup in Add a new row or Update a row with the entity set name and GUID, handle customer and owner lookups, and clear a lookup with Unrelate rows.

faqs.question: How do I set a lookup column in Power Automate for Dataverse?
faqs.answer: Enter the related table's entity set name followed by the row's GUID in brackets, for example accounts(0f8fad5b-d9cb-469f-a165-70867728950e).

faqs.question: How do I clear a Dataverse lookup in a flow?
faqs.answer: Use the Unrelate rows action with the lookup's relationship and the URL of the currently related row.

faqs.question: Where do I find the entity set name?
faqs.answer: In the table's properties under Advanced options as the logical collection name. It is usually the plural logical name, such as accounts or cnt_projects.

title: Limit Dataverse triggers with select columns and filter rows
shortDescription: Make 'When a row is added, modified or deleted' fire only for the columns and rows that matter, and stop a flow retriggering itself.
fullDescription: The Dataverse trigger fires on every change to a row unless told otherwise. Select columns limits it to changes in named columns. Filter rows limits it to rows that match a condition after the change. Together they cut run counts, prevent loops and make the flow's purpose clear.
problemStatement: A flow meant to react to a status change runs on every edit to the row, including its own updates, and burns through the daily request allowance.
whenToUse: Flows that should react to a change in one or two columns
Flows that update the row that triggered them
High-volume tables where most changes are irrelevant
whenNotToUse: Logic that needs the previous value of a column, which the trigger does not provide
Deletes, where only the row ID is available and Filter rows does not apply
formulaOrCode:
Trigger: Microsoft Dataverse > When a row is added, modified or deleted
  Change type:     Added or Modified
  Table name:      Service Requests
  Scope:           Organization          (User, Business unit, Parent: Child business unit, Organization)
  Select columns:  cnt_status,cnt_priority
                   Comma separated logical names. The flow runs only when one of these columns is in the update.
                   Applies to Modified. Added always fires.
  Filter rows:     cnt_status eq 100000002 and statecode eq 0
                   OData filter evaluated on the row after the change.
  Delay until:     @{addMinutes(utcNow(), 5)}      optional, postpones the run
  Run as:          Flow owner | Modifying user | Row owner      whose permissions the Dataverse actions use

Stop self-triggering
  The flow updates cnt_processedon on the same row.
  Keep cnt_processedon OUT of Select columns. The update then does not match and the trigger does not fire again.
  If the flow must update a watched column, add a guard to Filter rows:
    cnt_status eq 100000002 and cnt_processedon eq null

React to a specific transition (old value to new value)
  The trigger gives only current values. Options:
  1. Store the last processed value in a column and compare:
       Filter rows: cnt_status ne cnt_laststatus is not valid OData between two columns, so compare in a trigger
       condition instead (Settings > Trigger conditions):
       @not(equals(triggerOutputs()?['body/cnt_status'], triggerOutputs()?['body/cnt_laststatus']))
  2. Turn on auditing and read the audit history for the old value when needed.

Who made the change
  triggerOutputs()?['body/_modifiedby_value']
  Skip changes made by the flow's own account with a trigger condition:
  @not(equals(triggerOutputs()?['body/_modifiedby_value'], '<service account systemuserid>'))

Useful trigger outputs
  triggerOutputs()?['body/cnt_servicerequestid']                       row ID
  triggerOutputs()?['body/SdkMessage']                                 Create, Update or Delete
  triggerOutputs()?['body/cnt_status@OData.Community.Display.V1.FormattedValue']    choice label

Scope matters
  User scope fires only for rows owned by the flow owner. Use Organization for process flows.
stepByStepInstructions: Set the change type to what the flow needs.
List the columns that should start the flow in Select columns.
Add a Filter rows condition for the row state you care about.
Keep any column the flow writes out of Select columns, or guard it in the filter.
Set Scope to Organization for flows that serve everyone.
Edit an unrelated column on a test row and confirm no run starts.
commonMistakes: Leaving Select columns empty on a flow that updates its own row.
Using display names in Select columns.
Leaving Scope on User, so the flow runs only for the owner's rows.
Expecting Filter rows to see the old value.
troubleshooting: If the flow does not fire, check the scope, then test the filter in a List rows action to see whether the row matches.
If it fires twice, another process updates a watched column. Check the modified-by value in each run.
If it loops, a column the flow updates is in Select columns.
If saving the trigger fails, a name in Select columns is not a valid logical name.
seoTitle: Limit Dataverse triggers with select columns and filter rows
seoDescription: Make 'When a row is added, modified or deleted' fire only for the columns and rows that matter, and stop a flow retriggering itself.
primaryKeyword: Dataverse trigger select columns filter rows

faqs.question: How do I trigger a flow only when one Dataverse column changes?
faqs.answer: Enter the column's logical name in the trigger's Select columns field. The flow then runs only when that column is part of the update.

faqs.question: How do I stop a Dataverse flow triggering itself?
faqs.answer: Do not include the columns the flow updates in Select columns, or add a Filter rows condition that is false after the flow has run.

faqs.question: Can the Dataverse trigger give me the previous value?
faqs.answer: No. It returns the current row. Keep the last value in another column or read it from audit history.

title: Count and sum Dataverse rows with FetchXML in Power Automate
shortDescription: Use the Fetch Xml Query field of List rows to return counts, sums and grouped totals from Dataverse without looping through rows.
fullDescription: OData filters return rows. FetchXML can return answers: how many open requests per owner, the total value per month, the latest date per account. The List rows action accepts FetchXML directly, so a flow can get a summary in one call and a few rows instead of thousands.
problemStatement: A weekly summary flow lists 30,000 rows and counts them with variables inside Apply to each. It takes an hour and sometimes times out.
whenToUse: Digest emails and dashboards that need counts or totals
Checking whether any matching rows exist before doing work
Queries with joins or conditions OData cannot express
whenNotToUse: Simple filtered lists, where Filter rows is easier to read
Aggregates over more than 50,000 rows, which hit the aggregate limit and need narrower filters
formulaOrCode:
List rows > Table name: Service Requests > Fetch Xml Query:

Count of open requests
<fetch aggregate="true">
  <entity name="cnt_servicerequest">
    <attribute name="cnt_servicerequestid" alias="total" aggregate="count" />
    <filter><condition attribute="statecode" operator="eq" value="0" /></filter>
  </entity>
</fetch>
Read: first(outputs('List_rows')?['body/value'])?['total']

Count and sum grouped by owner
<fetch aggregate="true">
  <entity name="cnt_servicerequest">
    <attribute name="ownerid" alias="owner" groupby="true" />
    <attribute name="cnt_servicerequestid" alias="requests" aggregate="count" />
    <attribute name="cnt_amount" alias="amount" aggregate="sum" />
    <filter><condition attribute="statecode" operator="eq" value="0" /></filter>
    <order alias="requests" descending="true" />
  </entity>
</fetch>
Each item:  item()?['owner@OData.Community.Display.V1.FormattedValue']   item()?['requests']   item()?['amount']

Grouped by month created
    <attribute name="createdon" alias="month" groupby="true" dategrouping="month" />
    <attribute name="createdon" alias="year" groupby="true" dategrouping="year" />
    dategrouping: day | week | month | quarter | year | fiscal-period | fiscal-year

Other aggregates:  aggregate="avg" | "min" | "max" | "countcolumn" (non-null values)   distinct="true"

Join to a parent and filter on it
<fetch aggregate="true">
  <entity name="cnt_servicerequest">
    <attribute name="cnt_servicerequestid" alias="total" aggregate="count" />
    <link-entity name="account" from="accountid" to="cnt_account" alias="acc">
      <attribute name="name" alias="account" groupby="true" />
      <filter><condition attribute="address1_country" operator="eq" value="UK" /></filter>
    </link-entity>
  </entity>
</fetch>

Date operators (no calculation needed)
  operator="today" | "last-x-days" value="7" | "this-month" | "last-month" | "older-than-x-days" value="30" | "next-x-days" value="14"

Dynamic values: insert flow expressions inside the XML
  <condition attribute="ownerid" operator="eq" value="@{triggerOutputs()?['body/_ownerid_value']}" />
  Escape text with replace() for & < > and quotes if it comes from users.

Top rows without aggregation
<fetch top="10"> ... <order attribute="createdon" descending="true" /> ... </fetch>

Build queries visually: model-driven Advanced find > Download FetchXML, or XrmToolBox FetchXML Builder.
Aggregate limit: 50,000 rows contribute to one aggregate query. Narrow the filter if you hit AggregateQueryRecordLimit.
stepByStepInstructions: Build the query in Advanced find or FetchXML Builder and test it.
Add aggregate="true" to the fetch element and an alias to every attribute.
Paste the XML into the Fetch Xml Query field of List rows.
Replace fixed values with flow expressions where needed.
Read results by alias from the action's value array.
Feed grouped results into Create HTML table for a digest.
commonMistakes: Leaving out the alias on an aggregated attribute.
Mixing aggregated and non-grouped plain attributes in one query.
Filling Filter rows as well as Fetch Xml Query in the same action.
Summing a currency column across rows in different currencies without using the base column.
troubleshooting: If you get 'An attribute can not be requested when an aggregate operation has been specified', every attribute needs aggregate or groupby.
If the result is empty rather than zero, no rows matched. Use coalesce(first(...)?['total'], 0).
If you hit the aggregate record limit, add date or status filters and combine several smaller queries.
If the lookup group shows a GUID, read the FormattedValue annotation for the name.
seoTitle: Count and sum Dataverse rows with FetchXML in Power Automate
seoDescription: Use the Fetch Xml Query field of List rows to return counts, sums and grouped totals from Dataverse without looping through rows.

faqs.question: Can Power Automate count Dataverse rows without a loop?
faqs.answer: Yes. Put an aggregate FetchXML query with aggregate="count" in the List rows action's Fetch Xml Query field and read the alias from the first result.

faqs.question: How do I group results in FetchXML?
faqs.answer: Add groupby="true" to the attribute to group on, and give every attribute an alias.

faqs.question: What is the row limit for FetchXML aggregates?
faqs.answer: An aggregate query can cover up to 50,000 rows. Beyond that it fails, so filter to a smaller set.

title: Patch customer, owner and regarding lookups in a canvas app
shortDescription: Read and write Dataverse lookups that can point at more than one table, such as Customer, Owner and Regarding, with IsType and AsType.
fullDescription: Some Dataverse lookups accept rows from several tables. Customer can be an account or a contact. Owner can be a user or a team. Regarding can be almost anything. Power Fx treats these as record references: you can patch any allowed record into them, but to read columns you must first say which table the row belongs to.
problemStatement: A gallery shows nothing for the customer's name, or the formula bar reports that the column cannot be used, because the lookup's table is not known until run time.
whenToUse: Showing or setting Customer on cases, opportunities or custom tables
Assigning rows to users or teams
Linking activities and notes to parent rows
whenNotToUse: Ordinary single-table lookups, which need none of this
Filtering large tables by a polymorphic lookup's columns, which is not delegable
stepByStepInstructions: Add each table the lookup can point to as a data source.
Patch the lookup with a whole record from one of those tables.
Use IsType to test which table a row's lookup refers to.
Use AsType to read columns once the type is known.
Filter by comparing the lookup with a record.
Test with rows of each type and with a blank lookup.
commonMistakes: Reading .Name directly from a polymorphic lookup.
Patching a GUID or text into the lookup.
Forgetting to add Teams as a data source when owners can be teams.
Calling AsType without checking IsType, which errors on rows of the other type.
troubleshooting: If AsType fails for some rows, they point at a different table. Guard with IsType.
If Owner patches fail, the target user needs a security role with read access to the table.
If the gallery is slow, AsType runs per row. Show the lookup's name through a view column or cache the related tables.
If Regarding cannot be set, the parent table must have notes or activities enabled.
seoTitle: Patch customer, owner and regarding lookups in a canvas app
seoDescription: Read and write Dataverse lookups that can point at more than one table, such as Customer, Owner and Regarding, with IsType and AsType.

faqs.question: How do I patch the Customer column in Power Apps?
faqs.answer: Pass a whole account or contact record, for example Patch(Cases, ThisItem, { Customer: cmbAccount.Selected }).

faqs.question: How do I show the name from a polymorphic lookup?
faqs.answer: Check the type with IsType, then use AsType to read the name: AsType(ThisItem.Customer, Accounts).'Account Name'.

faqs.question: How do I change the owner of a Dataverse row from a canvas app?
faqs.answer: Patch the Owner column with a record from the Users or Teams table.

title: Upload and show Dataverse file and image columns in a canvas app
shortDescription: Store documents and pictures on a Dataverse row with file and image columns, using the form's attachment control, Patch and the camera.
fullDescription: File and image columns keep a document or picture on the row itself, with Dataverse security applied. In a canvas app the simplest route is an Edit form, which gives each file column an upload control. Images can also be patched directly from the camera or an Add picture control.
problemStatement: Files are pushed into SharePoint from a Dataverse app through a flow, which splits security in two and leaves orphaned documents when rows are deleted.
whenToUse: One document or photo per column per row, such as a signed form or profile picture
Files that should follow the row's security
Photos taken on a phone in the field
whenNotToUse: Many files per row or files needing versioning and co-authoring, which belong in SharePoint
Files above the column's configured size limit
formulaOrCode:
Columns
  File column:   Data type File. Maximum size 32 MB by default (32768 KB), configurable up to 10 GB.
  Image column:  Data type Image. Up to 30 MB. "Can store full images" keeps the original as well as the thumbnail.
                 One image column can be marked Primary image and is shown in model-driven headers.

Edit form (simplest)
  Insert > Edit form > Data source: Service Requests > add the file column as a field.
  The card contains an attachment-style control: users select a file, SubmitForm(frmRequest) uploads it.
  One file per file column. Selecting another replaces it.

Show or download a file
  // Label with the name
  ThisItem.'Signed Form'.FileName
  // Download button OnSelect
  Download(ThisItem.'Signed Form'.Value)
  // PDF viewer Document
  ThisItem.'Signed Form'.Value

Patch a file from an attachment control outside a form
  // attUpload is an attachment control copied from a form, MaxAttachments = 1
  Patch(
      'Service Requests', gblSelectedRequest,
      { 'Signed Form': { FileName: First(attUpload.Attachments).Name, Value: First(attUpload.Attachments).Value } }
  )
  // Remove the file
  Patch('Service Requests', gblSelectedRequest, { 'Signed Form': Blank() })

Images
  // Show (thumbnail by default)
  Image.Image : ThisItem.Photo
  // Full size
  Image.Image : ThisItem.Photo.Full
  // Save from the camera
  Patch('Service Requests', gblSelectedRequest, { Photo: camCapture.Photo })
  // Save from Add picture
  Patch('Service Requests', gblSelectedRequest, { Photo: imgUploaded.Image })
  // Clear
  Patch('Service Requests', gblSelectedRequest, { Photo: Blank() })

Galleries
  Show thumbnails (ThisItem.Photo) in rows and load .Full only on the detail screen.

Power Automate
  Download a file or an image:  Dataverse > Download a file or an image (row ID + column)
  Upload:                       Dataverse > Upload a file or an image (row ID + column + content + file name)
  Email as an attachment:       Attachments Name = file name, Content = body of the download action

Notes on a row (many files) as the alternative
  Patch(Notes, Defaults(Notes), { Title: "Photo", Regarding: gblSelectedRequest, ... }) is limited from canvas.
  For multiple files, use the form's built-in Attachments card (Notes) on tables with attachments enabled.
stepByStepInstructions: Add a file or image column to the table and set its size limit.
Add the column to an Edit form to get the upload control.
Save with SubmitForm, or Patch the file record from an attachment control.
Show the file name with a download button, and images with an Image control.
Use thumbnails in galleries and the full image on detail screens.
Use the Dataverse upload and download actions when a flow needs the file.
commonMistakes: Using file columns for many documents per row.
Loading full-size images in every gallery row.
Patching text or a URL into a file column.
Forgetting that file columns are not copied by simple row duplication or some import tools.
troubleshooting: If upload fails on large files, raise the column's maximum size or reduce the file.
If the image looks blurry, you are showing the thumbnail. Use .Full where the column stores full images.
If Download does nothing on mobile, open the file in a PDF viewer control or launch it through a flow-generated link.
If the file card is missing in the form, refresh the data source after adding the column.
seoTitle: Upload and show Dataverse file and image columns in a canvas app
seoDescription: Store documents and pictures on a Dataverse row with file and image columns, using the form's attachment control, Patch and the camera.
primaryKeyword: Power Apps Dataverse file column upload

faqs.question: How do I upload a file to Dataverse from a canvas app?
faqs.answer: Add the file column to an Edit form and submit the form, or patch a record with FileName and Value taken from an attachment control.

faqs.question: How big can a Dataverse file column be?
faqs.answer: The limit is set per column. The default is 32 MB and it can be raised to as much as 10 GB.

faqs.question: Should I use a file column or SharePoint?
faqs.answer: Use a file column for one document per purpose that should share the row's security. Use SharePoint for many files, versioning and co-authoring.

title: Use Dataverse views as filters in a canvas app
shortDescription: Point a gallery at a Dataverse system or personal view so complex filters live in the view, stay delegable and can be changed without editing the app.
fullDescription: A Dataverse view is a saved query. A canvas app can use one as the first argument's filter, which pushes the whole view definition to the server. Conditions that are awkward or non-delegable in Power Fx, such as filters on related tables or relative dates, become a single delegable call.
problemStatement: A gallery formula with six conditions shows a delegation warning, and every change to the business rule means editing and republishing the app.
whenToUse: Filters involving related tables or relative dates
Rules that administrators adjust from time to time
Offering users the same lists they know from the model-driven app
whenNotToUse: Filters driven by controls on the screen, which still need Power Fx conditions
Views whose columns matter, since the app decides its own columns
formulaOrCode:
Syntax
  Filter(<table>, <table> (Views).'<view name>')

Examples
  // Gallery of active requests, as defined by the system view
  Filter('Service Requests', 'Service Requests (Views)'.'Active Service Requests')
