  // The built-in "my rows" view
  Filter(Accounts, 'Accounts (Views)'.'My Active Accounts')

  // Add screen-driven conditions on top (all delegated together)
  Filter(
      'Service Requests',
      'Service Requests (Views)'.'Overdue Requests',
      StartsWith(Subject, txtSearch.Text),
      Priority = ddPriority.Selected.Value
  )

  // Sort the result
  SortByColumns(
      Filter('Service Requests', 'Service Requests (Views)'.'Overdue Requests'),
      "cnt_duedate", SortOrder.Ascending
  )

  // Count (delegable up to 50,000 rows)
  CountRows(Filter('Service Requests', 'Service Requests (Views)'.'Overdue Requests'))

Let the user pick a view
  // ddView.Items
  Table(
      { Label: "Active",  View: 'Service Requests (Views)'.'Active Service Requests' },
      { Label: "Overdue", View: 'Service Requests (Views)'.'Overdue Requests' },
      { Label: "Mine",    View: 'Service Requests (Views)'.'My Open Requests' }
  )
  // galRequests.Items
  Filter('Service Requests', ddView.Selected.View)

What the view contributes
  Its filter conditions, including conditions on related tables and operators such as "Last 7 days",
  "Equals current user" and "Under" for hierarchies.
  Not its columns or sort order. Sort in the app.

Creating the view
  Maker portal > Table > Views > New view > add filters > Save and publish.
  Add the view to your solution. After creating a new view, refresh the table's data source in the app
  so the name appears.

Personal views
  Views a user saved for themselves appear in the same (Views) enumeration for that user only. Do not
  build app logic on them.
stepByStepInstructions: Create or choose a system view that expresses the filter.
In the app, refresh the table's data source.
Use the view as a Filter argument with the (Views) enumeration.
Add further screen-driven conditions as extra Filter arguments.
Sort in the app with SortByColumns.
Change the view in the maker portal when the rule changes, with no app edit.
commonMistakes: Expecting the gallery to follow the view's sort order and columns.
Renaming a view, which breaks the formula that names it.
Using a personal view in an app shared with others.
Rebuilding in Power Fx a filter that already exists as a view.
troubleshooting: If the view name is not offered, refresh the data source or check the view is published.
If the app errors after a deployment, the view is missing from the solution in that environment.
If results differ from the model-driven app, the view was edited but not published.
If a delegation warning remains, it comes from the extra Power Fx conditions, not the view.
seoTitle: Use Dataverse views as filters in a canvas app
seoDescription: Point a gallery at a Dataverse system or personal view so complex filters live in the view, stay delegable and can be changed without editing the app.

faqs.question: Can a canvas app use a Dataverse view?
faqs.answer: Yes. Use Filter(Table, 'Table (Views)'.'View name'). The view's conditions run on the server.

faqs.question: Are Dataverse views delegable in Power Apps?
faqs.answer: Yes. The whole view filter is delegated, including conditions on related tables.

faqs.question: Does the gallery use the view's columns and sorting?
faqs.answer: No. Only the filter is applied. Choose columns and sorting in the app.

title: Bind Dataverse choice columns to drop-downs and combo boxes
shortDescription: Fill a control from a Dataverse choice column with Choices(), set its default, save single and multi-select values, and filter a gallery by the selection.
fullDescription: Dataverse choices are typed values, not text. A control bound with Choices() always shows the current options, labels follow the user's language, and comparisons use the choice value itself. This covers the full round trip: items, default, save and filter.
problemStatement: The drop-down is filled with a hand-typed list of labels, so it breaks when an option is added or renamed, and filters compare text that does not match.
whenToUse: Any form or filter bar that edits or filters on a choice column
Apps used in more than one language
whenNotToUse: Lists that business users must maintain themselves, which should be a lookup table
Very long lists, where a searchable lookup is easier to use
stepByStepInstructions: Set the control's Items to Choices() for the column.
Set the default from the selected record, falling back to a sensible option.
Patch the control's selected value, or SelectedItems for multi-select.
Filter galleries by comparing the column with the selected choice.
Use Text() to display the label.
Refresh the data source after options are added in Dataverse.
commonMistakes: Typing option labels as text in Items.
Comparing a choice column with a string.
Using Default on a combo box, which needs DefaultSelectedItems.
Patching .Selected.Value.Value or other guessed shapes.
troubleshooting: If a new option does not appear, refresh the table in the Data pane.
If the filter returns nothing, compare with the enum or the control's Selected.Value, not text.
If the default is blank on edit, the record variable is not set before the screen opens.
If labels show in the wrong language, they follow the user's Dataverse language setting.
seoTitle: Bind Dataverse choice columns to drop-downs and combo boxes
seoDescription: Fill a control from a Dataverse choice column with Choices(), set its default, save single and multi-select values, and filter a gallery by the selection.

faqs.question: How do I populate a dropdown from a Dataverse choice column?
faqs.answer: Set the control's Items property to Choices('Table'.Column).

faqs.question: How do I patch a Dataverse choice column from a dropdown?
faqs.answer: Patch the control's Selected.Value, for example { Priority: ddPriority.Selected.Value }.

faqs.question: How do I filter by a choice column in Power Apps?
faqs.answer: Compare the column with the choice value: Filter(Table, Priority = ddPriority.Selected.Value). This is delegable.

title: Protect sensitive Dataverse columns with column security profiles
shortDescription: Hide or lock individual columns such as salary or national ID with column-level security, so only members of a profile can read or change them.
fullDescription: Security roles decide which rows a user can reach. Column security decides which columns on those rows they can see. Turn it on for a sensitive column and only users or teams in a column security profile get the value. Everyone else sees it blank in apps, flows, exports and the API.
problemStatement: A sensitive value is 'hidden' by leaving it off the form, but anyone with access to the row can still read it in a view, an export or a canvas app.
whenToUse: Personal or financial values on otherwise widely shared rows
Columns only a few roles may edit, such as approval limits
whenNotToUse: Hiding whole rows, which is the job of security roles and ownership
Columns used as alternate keys or required by integrations running as ordinary users
formulaOrCode:
1. Secure the column
   Table > Columns > open the column > Advanced options > Enable column security: On
   Works for most custom columns and some system columns. Not available for the primary key, some lookups
   and formula columns.

2. Create a profile
   Power Platform admin centre > Environments > (env) > Settings > Users + permissions > Column security profiles
   New profile: "HR - Salary"
   Column permissions > select the column >
     Read:    Allowed
     Update:  Allowed | Not allowed
     Create:  Allowed | Not allowed
   Newer environments also offer masked read, where a masking rule shows part of the value.

3. Add members
   Profile > Users or Teams > Add. Prefer teams linked to Entra security groups.
   System Administrators always have full access to secured columns.

4. Add the profile and the column to your solution so both deploy together.

What other users experience
   Model-driven form:   field shows ******** with a key icon, read-only
   Views and exports:   empty
   Canvas app:          value is blank. Patch to the column fails with a permission error.
   Flow:                value is null for connections without access. Updates fail.
   Web API:             the property is omitted or null

Canvas app: adapt the screen instead of showing an empty box
   // Is the value readable for me? (works when the column is normally filled)
   // conSalary.Visible
   !IsBlank(gblSelectedEmployee.Salary) || nfIsHr
   // Check access explicitly with the security role pattern, then hide or disable the card.
   // Do not rely on hiding alone: the profile is what protects the data.

Share one row's secured column with one person (model-driven)
   Row > Share secured field: grant read or update on that column for that row only.
   Stored in the Field Sharing (principalobjectattributeaccess) table.

Flows and integrations
   The connection's user must be in a profile that allows what the flow does. Add the service account or
   application user to the profile, or the flow silently writes nulls and reads blanks.

Audit
   Turn on auditing for the column to record who changed it. Reads are not audited by column security;
   use Purview activity logging for read auditing where licensed.
stepByStepInstructions: Identify the sensitive columns and who needs to read or change them.
Enable column security on each column.
Create a profile per audience and set read, update and create permissions.
Add teams or users to each profile.
Add service accounts used by flows to the profiles they need.
Test with a user outside the profile in the app, a view and an export.
commonMistakes: Relying on form layout to hide sensitive values.
Securing a column and forgetting the flow account, so automation writes blanks.
Adding individuals to profiles instead of teams.
Leaving the profile out of the solution.
troubleshooting: If a flow suddenly reads null, its connection user is not in the profile.
If a user in the profile still sees asterisks, check the profile grants Read and that team membership has synced.
If Patch fails with a privilege message naming the column, the user lacks Update or Create in the profile.
If column security cannot be enabled, the column type does not support it. Move the value to a related table with tighter role access.
seoTitle: Protect sensitive Dataverse columns with column security profiles
seoDescription: Hide or lock individual columns such as salary or national ID with column-level security, so only members of a profile can read or change them.

faqs.question: How do I hide a column from some users in Dataverse?
faqs.answer: Enable column security on the column, then create a column security profile that grants read to the users or teams allowed to see it.

faqs.question: Do system administrators bypass column security?
faqs.answer: Yes. Users with the System Administrator role can read and update all secured columns.

faqs.question: Does column security apply in canvas apps and flows?
faqs.answer: Yes. It is enforced by Dataverse for every client, so the value is blank for users and connections without access.

title: Share Dataverse rows with owner teams and access teams
shortDescription: Choose between team ownership, Entra group teams, access teams and row sharing to give the right people access to specific rows without widening security roles.
fullDescription: User-level roles limit people to their own rows. Real work needs colleagues to see some of each other's rows. Dataverse offers four tools for that. Owner teams own rows and carry roles. Entra group teams do the same with membership managed in Entra. Access teams grant access per row with no ownership change. Sharing grants one user or team access to one row.
problemStatement: To let a project group see each other's rows, everyone's Read privilege is raised to Organization, exposing every row to everyone.
whenToUse: Rows that a department or queue should work on together
Rows that need an ad hoc group, such as a deal team
Giving one person access to one row
whenNotToUse: Sharing thousands of rows individually, which slows queries through the access table
Access teams when every row needs the same people, where an owner team is simpler
formulaOrCode:
Choosing
  Same group for many rows, group should own them        Owner team (or Entra group team)
  Membership managed by IT in Entra                      Entra ID security group team / Office group team
  Different people per row, owner stays the same          Access team (template on the table)
  One-off access for a person or team to one row          Share

Owner team
  Admin centre > Environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Teams > New: type Owner
  Assign a security role to the team. Add members.
  Assign rows to the team (Owner = team).
  Members get the team's role privileges. With User-level Read in the team's role, members can read rows
  the team owns.
  Role setting "Member's privilege inheritance":
    Team privileges only                               members act through the team
    Direct User (Basic) access level and Team privileges   members also get the privileges personally,
                                                        so they can own rows without a personal role

Entra group team
  Team type: Microsoft Entra ID Security Group (or Office Group) > pick the group > Membership type: Members
  Membership is applied when a user next signs in or is impersonated. No manual upkeep.

Access team (per row)
  1. Table > Properties > Advanced options > Have an access team: On
  2. Settings > Access team templates > New: table, access rights (Read, Write, Append, Append To, Delete, Share, Assign)
  3. Model-driven form: add a sub-grid of Users > Team template: your template
  4. Adding a user to the sub-grid creates the row's team automatically and grants those rights for that row.
  From a flow: Perform a bound action on the row
     Action name: AddUserToRecordTeam
     Record:      the row
     SystemUser@odata.id / TeamTemplate: systemusers(<guid>) and teamtemplates(<template guid>)
  Remove: RemoveUserFromRecordTeam

Share one row
  Model-driven: Share > add user or team > tick rights
  Flow: Dataverse > Perform an unbound action > GrantAccess
     Target:            { "@odata.type": "Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.cnt_servicerequest", "cnt_servicerequestid": "<guid>" }
     PrincipalAccess:   { "Principal": { "@odata.type": "Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.systemuser", "systemuserid": "<guid>" },
                          "AccessMask": "ReadAccess, WriteAccess, AppendAccess" }
  Revoke: RevokeAccess with Target and Revokee.
  Sharing only works within the privileges the recipient's roles already grant on the table (at least User level).

Canvas app
  Assign to a team:  Patch('Service Requests', ThisItem, { Owner: LookUp(Teams, 'Team Name' = "Support Tier 2") })
  My team's rows:    visible automatically when the role grants User-level Read and the team owns the row.

Check who has access to a row
  Model-driven: command bar > Check access (shows roles, team memberships and shares that grant it).
stepByStepInstructions: List who needs access to which rows and whether the group is fixed or per row.
Pick owner team, Entra group team, access team or sharing using the guide above.
Create the team or template and assign roles or rights.
Change row ownership or add members to the row's access team.
Keep table privileges at User level so access comes only through ownership, teams and shares.
Verify with Check access on a sample row.
commonMistakes: Raising Read to Organization to solve a team access problem.
Sharing every row individually from a flow at high volume.
Forgetting the team needs a security role before it can own rows.
Expecting sharing to work for users with no privilege on the table at all.
troubleshooting: If a team cannot be set as owner, assign it a role with privileges on the table.
If Entra group members do not get access, they must sign in after being added, and the role inheritance setting must suit your design.
If an access team sub-grid adds users but access is missing, check the template's rights and the user's base privilege.
If queries slow down, review the number of shares in the principal object access table and move to teams.
seoTitle: Share Dataverse rows with owner teams and access teams
seoDescription: Choose between team ownership, Entra group teams, access teams and row sharing to give the right people access to specific rows without widening security roles.
primaryKeyword: Dataverse access team vs owner team

faqs.question: What is the difference between an owner team and an access team?
faqs.answer: An owner team owns rows and has security roles. An access team owns nothing and has no roles. It grants its members rights on individual rows through a template.

faqs.question: How do I share a Dataverse record with another user from a flow?
faqs.answer: Call the GrantAccess action with the target row, the user or team and the access mask.

faqs.question: Should I use Entra group teams?
faqs.answer: Yes, for stable groups. Membership is managed once in Entra and applied to Dataverse automatically.

title: Turn on Dataverse auditing and read change history
shortDescription: Enable auditing at environment, table and column level, view who changed what on a row, read the audit log from a flow, and manage how long logs are kept.
fullDescription: Dataverse can record every create, update and delete with the old value, the new value, the user and the time. It only does so when auditing is switched on at three levels. Once on, the history appears on each row in model-driven apps and can be queried for reports, investigations and flows that need a previous value.
problemStatement: Someone asks who changed a request's amount last month. Auditing was never enabled, so there is no answer.
whenToUse: Business data where changes must be attributable
Flows that need the previous value of a column
whenNotToUse: High-churn technical tables such as logs, where audit rows multiply storage for no benefit
Treating audit as a backup. It records changes, it does not restore deleted rows by itself
formulaOrCode:
Enable (all three levels are required)
  1. Environment: Power Platform admin centre > Environments > (env) > Settings > Audit and logs > Audit settings
       Start Auditing: On        Log access: optional        Read logs: optional (also sends to Purview)
       Retain these logs for: 30 days | 90 | 180 | 1 year | 2 years | 7 years | Custom | Forever
  2. Table: Table > Properties > Advanced options > Audit changes to its data: On
  3. Column: each column > Advanced options > Enable auditing: On (default on for new columns)
  Publish. Include table settings in your solution so auditing is on in every environment.

View
  Model-driven app > open a row > Related > Audit History: changed date, changed by, event, field, old value, new value
  Admin centre > Environment > Settings > Audit and logs > Audit summary view: filter by table, user, event

Read from a flow: who last changed a column and what it was
  List rows > Table: Audits
    Filter rows:  _objectid_value eq @{triggerOutputs()?['body/cnt_servicerequestid']} and action eq 2
    Sort by:      createdon desc        Row count: 5
    action: 1 Create, 2 Update, 3 Delete        operation: 1 Create, 2 Update, 3 Delete, 4 Access
  The row gives who (_userid_value) and when (createdon). Old and new values are in the audit detail:
  HTTP (Invoke an HTTP request) GET
    /api/data/v9.2/audits(<auditid>)/Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.RetrieveAuditDetails()
  Response: AuditDetail.OldValue and AuditDetail.NewValue hold only the changed columns.

Full history for one row
  GET /api/data/v9.2/RetrieveRecordChangeHistory(Target=@t)?@t={'@odata.id':'cnt_servicerequests(<guid>)'}

Storage
  Audit data is stored in Log capacity, separate from Database capacity. See usage in
  admin centre > Resources > Capacity > Dataverse > Log.
  Reduce it: set a retention period (old logs are deleted automatically), turn off auditing on noisy columns
  such as last-synced timestamps, and delete logs by table, date or user from
  Audit settings > Delete logs.

What is and is not recorded
  Recorded: create, update (changed columns only), delete, assign, share, role changes, user access when enabled.
  Not recorded: reads of individual rows unless Read logs is on, changes while auditing was off,
  values of columns with auditing disabled, file contents.

Permissions
  View Audit History and View Audit Summary are privileges on the security role (Core Records > Miscellaneous).
stepByStepInstructions: Turn on auditing for the environment and choose a retention period.
Enable auditing on each business table.
Review columns and switch auditing off for noisy technical ones.
Grant View Audit History to the roles that need it.
Check a row's audit history after a test edit.
Monitor log capacity and adjust retention.
commonMistakes: Enabling the table but not the environment setting, so nothing is recorded.
Keeping logs forever on high-volume tables.
Assuming changes made before auditing was enabled can be recovered.
Forgetting that the setting does not travel between environments unless the table is in the solution.
troubleshooting: If Audit History is empty, check all three levels and that the change happened after auditing was enabled.
If users cannot see the Audit History tab, add the View Audit History privilege to their role.
If log capacity is growing fast, find the noisiest table in the audit summary and narrow its audited columns.
If RetrieveAuditDetails returns 403, the caller needs audit view privileges.
seoTitle: Turn on Dataverse auditing and read change history
seoDescription: Enable auditing at environment, table and column level, view who changed what on a row, read the audit log from a flow, and manage how long logs are kept.

faqs.question: How do I see who changed a record in Dataverse?
faqs.answer: Open the row in a model-driven app and choose Related, then Audit History. Auditing must be enabled for the environment, the table and the column.

faqs.question: Does Dataverse auditing use database storage?
faqs.answer: No. Audit logs use log capacity, which is measured separately.

faqs.question: Can I get the old value of a column in Power Automate?
faqs.answer: Yes. Find the audit row for the change and call RetrieveAuditDetails to read the old and new values.

title: Prevent duplicate rows in Dataverse with keys and detection rules
shortDescription: Block exact duplicates with an alternate key, warn about likely duplicates with detection rules, and check before saving from a canvas app.
fullDescription: Dataverse has two tools for duplicates. An alternate key makes a combination of columns unique and rejects a second row outright, from any source. Duplicate detection rules look for near matches and warn the user in model-driven apps. Canvas apps and flows should check for themselves before creating rows.
problemStatement: The same customer exists four times with slightly different spellings, and nobody knows which row holds the real history.
whenToUse: Tables where a business identifier must be unique
Customer and contact data entered by many people
Imports that may contain rows already present
whenNotToUse: Keys on free-text names, which block legitimate rows and miss near matches
Detection rules as the only defence for data created by flows, since they are not enforced there by default
formulaOrCode:
1. Hard block: alternate key
   Table > Keys > New key > columns: cnt_RegistrationNumber   (or a combination: cnt_Email + cnt_Region)
   A second row with the same values is rejected:
     "A record that has the attribute values ... already exists. The entity key ... requires that this set of
      attributes contains unique values."  (error 0x80060892)
   Blank values: rows where a key column is blank are not treated as duplicates of each other.

2. Soft warning: duplicate detection rules (model-driven apps)
   Admin centre > Environment > Settings > Data management > Duplicate detection settings: enable
     "When a record is created or updated" and "During data import"
   Duplicate detection rules > New
     Base record type: Contact      Matching record type: Contact
     Criteria:  Email   Exact match
                Last Name  Same first characters: 5       First Name  Same first characters: 1
     Exclude inactive matching records: Yes
   Publish the rule. Up to 5 published rules per table. Rules are unpublished by solution import: republish.
   Users see "Duplicate records found" and can save anyway or cancel.

3. Canvas app: check before create
   // btnSave.OnSelect
   With(
       { existing: LookUp(Contacts, Email = Lower(Trim(txtEmail.Text))) },
       If(
           !IsBlank(existing),
           UpdateContext({ locDuplicate: existing, locShowDuplicate: true }),
           IfError(
               Patch(Contacts, Defaults(Contacts), { 'First Name': txtFirst.Text, 'Last Name': txtLast.Text, Email: Lower(Trim(txtEmail.Text)) });
               Notify("Contact created", NotificationType.Success),
               Notify(If("already exists" in FirstError.Message, "A contact with these details already exists.", FirstError.Message), NotificationType.Error)
           )
       )
   )
   // Dialog offers: open the existing row, or create anyway (if policy allows)

4. Flow: upsert instead of create
   Update a row with an alternate key as the Row ID creates or updates in one step, so reruns cannot duplicate.
   To make detection rules apply to a Web API create, send header  MSCRM.SuppressDuplicateDetection: false

5. Clean existing duplicates
   Model-driven: Data management > Duplicate detection jobs > New: runs rules over existing rows.
   Review results, select two rows > Merge (accounts, contacts, leads, cases): choose the master and which
   values to keep. Child rows move to the master. The other row is deactivated.
   Custom tables have no merge: reparent children with a flow, then deactivate the duplicate.

Normalise before comparing
   Store emails lower-case and trimmed. Keep a cleaned key column (cnt_NameKey = Upper letters and digits only)
   and put the key or rule on that.
stepByStepInstructions: Decide which columns identify a row uniquely.
Add an alternate key for identifiers that must never repeat.
Enable duplicate detection and publish rules for near matches.
Add a lookup check before create in canvas apps.
Change import flows to upsert by key.
Run a detection job on existing data and merge or deactivate duplicates.
commonMistakes: Relying on detection rules for rows created by flows and canvas apps.
Putting a key on a column that already contains duplicates.
Forgetting to republish detection rules after a solution import.
Comparing emails without trimming and lower-casing.
troubleshooting: If the key fails to activate, remove existing duplicates in the key columns first.
If users are never warned, check the rule is published and detection on create and update is enabled.
If the canvas check misses a duplicate, values differ by case or spaces. Normalise both sides.
If the create error text is unclear to users, catch it with IfError and show a plain message.
seoTitle: Prevent duplicate rows in Dataverse with keys and detection rules
seoDescription: Block exact duplicates with an alternate key, warn about likely duplicates with detection rules, and check before saving from a canvas app.

faqs.question: How do I stop duplicate records in Dataverse?
faqs.answer: Create an alternate key on the columns that must be unique. Dataverse then rejects any row that repeats those values.

faqs.question: Do duplicate detection rules work in canvas apps?
faqs.answer: No. They warn users in model-driven apps and during imports. In a canvas app, check with LookUp before creating the row.

faqs.question: How do I merge duplicates?
faqs.answer: Select two accounts, contacts, leads or cases in a model-driven app and choose Merge. For custom tables, move child rows to the row you keep and deactivate the other.

title: Clean up Dataverse data with bulk delete jobs
shortDescription: Remove old rows on a schedule with bulk deletion jobs: logs, completed system jobs, old emails and test data, without writing a flow.
fullDescription: Deleting rows one by one from a flow is slow and uses API calls. A bulk deletion job runs inside Dataverse, takes a view-style filter, can repeat on a schedule and handles millions of rows. It is the standard tool for keeping storage under control.
problemStatement: Database capacity is nearly full. Most of it is years of system job history, flow run logs and a custom log table nobody trims.
whenToUse: Trimming log and history tables on a schedule
Storage clean-up of system jobs, emails with attachments and old audit-like tables
whenNotToUse: Business records under a retention obligation
Rows that should be archived rather than destroyed, where long-term retention policies fit better
formulaOrCode:
Create a job
  Power Platform admin centre > Environments > (env) > Settings > Data management > Bulk deletion > New
  1. Look for: the table.  Add filter rows, or pick a saved view under "Use saved view".
  2. Name the job. Start time.  Run this job after every: 7 | 30 | 90 | 180 | 365 days
  3. Send an email when finished (optional).
  The filter is re-evaluated on every run, so relative dates keep working.

Useful filters
  Custom log table        Created On    Older than X months: 3
  System jobs             Status Reason equals Succeeded   AND   Completed On   Older than X days: 30
                          System Job Type does not equal Bulk Delete
  Workflow / process sessions   Status equals Completed  AND  Completed On older than 30 days
  Emails with attachments Status Reason equals Completed  AND  Actual End older than X months: 12
                          (check with the business first)
  Import history          Import jobs: Created On older than 30 days
  Flow run history        FlowRun table (cloud flow run history in Dataverse) has its own TTL setting:
                          Organization table column FlowRunTimeToLiveInSeconds (default 28 days)
  Test rows               Created By equals <tester>  AND  Created On on or after <project start>

What happens
  Rows are deleted as the job's owner, respecting cascade rules: children with Parental or Cascade Delete go too.
  Restrict delete relationships cause failures for those rows.
  Plug-ins and flows triggered on delete DO run. Disable noisy "when a row is deleted" flows if needed.
  Deleted rows do not go to a recycle bin unless the environment's recycle bin (restore deleted rows)
  feature is on, where they can be restored for the configured period.

Monitor
  Bulk deletion list shows Successes and Failures per run. Open a job for the failure reasons.
  Storage figures in admin centre > Resources > Capacity update within about 24 hours.

From a flow or script (BulkDelete action)
  POST /api/data/v9.2/BulkDelete
  {
    "QuerySet": [ { "@odata.type": "Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.QueryExpression", "EntityName": "cnt_log",
        "Criteria": { "FilterOperator": "And", "Conditions": [
          { "AttributeName": "createdon", "Operator": "OlderThanXMonths", "Values": [ { "Value": 3, "Type": "System.Int32" } ] } ] } } ],
    "JobName": "Trim cnt_log", "SendEmailNotification": false, "RecurrencePattern": "FREQ=DAILY;INTERVAL=7",
    "StartDateTime": "2026-03-09T02:00:00Z", "ToRecipients": [], "CCRecipients": []
  }

Find what is using space first
  Admin centre > Resources > Capacity > (env) > details: top tables by size.
  Common large tables: AsyncOperationBase (system jobs), ActivityPointerBase and attachments, AuditBase (log capacity),
  WorkflowLogBase, custom log tables.
stepByStepInstructions: Check which tables use the most storage.
Agree what may be deleted and after how long.
Create a bulk deletion job with a filter and a recurrence.
Run it first with a narrow filter and review successes and failures.
Widen the filter and leave the recurring job in place.
Record the jobs in the environment's support notes.
commonMistakes: Deleting with a flow that loops over rows.
Forgetting cascade rules, so child rows vanish with their parents.
A filter with fixed dates that deletes nothing on later runs.
Running a first job across millions of rows in business hours.
troubleshooting: If rows fail to delete, a Restrict relationship or a plug-in blocked them. The job detail lists the reason.
If storage does not drop, wait a day for capacity figures, and check the large table is the one you trimmed.
If the job never starts, the async service is busy or the start time is in the future.
If the wrong rows were deleted, restore from the environment recycle bin if enabled, or from a backup to a copy environment.
seoTitle: Clean up Dataverse data with bulk delete jobs
seoDescription: Remove old rows on a schedule with bulk deletion jobs: logs, completed system jobs, old emails and test data, without writing a flow.

faqs.question: How do I delete many rows in Dataverse?
faqs.answer: Create a bulk deletion job in the environment's Data management settings with a filter for the rows, and optionally a recurrence.

faqs.question: Can bulk delete jobs run on a schedule?
faqs.answer: Yes. Set the job to run after every 7, 30, 90, 180 or 365 days. The filter is evaluated again each time.

faqs.question: Can I recover rows removed by a bulk delete?
faqs.answer: Only if the environment's recycle bin feature is enabled, or by restoring a backup to another environment and copying the rows back.

title: Choose the right Dataverse date behavior to avoid off-by-one-day errors
shortDescription: Pick User Local, Date Only or Time-Zone Independent for each date column, and handle the UTC values correctly in canvas apps and flows.
fullDescription: A date column in Dataverse has a behavior setting that decides whether values shift with the user's time zone. Choosing the wrong one makes a birthday appear a day early for some users, or a deadline move when a flow reads it. The setting can be changed in only limited ways later, so it is worth getting right at creation.
problemStatement: A date entered as 9 March shows as 8 March in a report, in an email from a flow, or for a colleague in another country.
whenToUse: Any new date or date and time column
Dates such as birthdays, contract dates and due dates that are the same everywhere
Timestamps of real events that should display in each user's local time
whenNotToUse: Changing behavior on a column full of data without planning a data fix
Storing dates as text to dodge the problem
formulaOrCode:
Behaviors
  User Local               Stored in UTC. Shown converted to each user's time zone.
                           Use for moments in time: created on, meeting start, approval timestamp.
  Date Only                Stored as a date with no time and no conversion. 9 March is 9 March for everyone.
                           Use for birthdays, due dates, contract start and end, holidays.
  Time-Zone Independent    Stored and shown exactly as entered, with a time, no conversion.
                           Use for local opening hours, hotel check-in, "08:00 at the site".

Format vs behavior
  Format "Date only" + behavior User Local = a UTC timestamp at the user's local midnight.
  This is the classic source of off-by-one errors: a UK user's 9 March 00:00 (GMT) is 8 March 19:00 in New York.
  For plain dates choose Format: Date only AND Behavior: Date Only.

Set it
  Column > Data type: Date and time or Date only > Advanced options > Time zone adjustment:
    User local | Date only | Time zone independent
  Changing later: User Local can be changed once to Date Only or Time-Zone Independent. Existing values are
  not converted, so they keep their UTC value. Other changes are not allowed.

Canvas app
  // App setting per column on date pickers: DateTimeZone = DateTimeZone.Local (default) or DateTimeZone.UTC
  // Date Only and Time-Zone Independent columns: Power Apps treats values as UTC.
  // Show without shifting:
  Text(ThisItem.'Contract Start', "d mmm yyyy", "en-GB")                 // Date Only columns display correctly
  // If a Time-Zone Independent value appears shifted, add the offset back:
  DateAdd(ThisItem.'Site Time', TimeZoneOffset(ThisItem.'Site Time'), TimeUnit.Minutes)
  // Filter by a Date Only column
  Filter('Service Requests', 'Due Date' = Today())
  // Filter by a User Local date and time column for "today"
  Filter('Service Requests', 'Created On' >= Today() && 'Created On' < DateAdd(Today(), 1, TimeUnit.Days))

Power Automate
  Date Only column returns  2026-03-09          Filter rows: cnt_duedate eq 2026-03-09
                            write with formatDateTime(<value>, 'yyyy-MM-dd')
  User Local column returns 2026-03-09T00:00:00Z (UTC)
                            show with convertFromUtc(<value>, 'GMT Standard Time', 'd MMMM yyyy HH:mm')
  "Today" for a Date Only column in a given zone:
     convertFromUtc(utcNow(), 'GMT Standard Time', 'yyyy-MM-dd')
  Overdue (Date Only): cnt_duedate lt @{convertFromUtc(utcNow(), 'GMT Standard Time', 'yyyy-MM-dd')}

Repair values after switching a column from User Local to Date Only
  Old rows hold UTC midnights of the entering user's zone. Run a one-off flow or script that converts each value
  to that zone's local date and writes it back.

Power BI and exports
  User Local columns arrive as UTC. Convert in the model. Date Only columns need no conversion.
stepByStepInstructions: Decide for each date whether it is a calendar date, a moment in time or a local wall-clock time.
Set format and behavior together when creating the column.
Use Date Only behavior for plain dates.
Convert User Local values to a named time zone in flows before showing them.
Test with two users in different time zones.
Plan a data fix before changing behavior on an existing column.
commonMistakes: Date-only format left with User Local behavior.
Formatting a UTC value in a flow without converting it.
Comparing a date and time column with Today() using equals.
Assuming every user shares the maker's time zone.
troubleshooting: If a date shows a day early, the column is User Local and the reader is west of the person who entered it. Switch to Date Only and repair the data.
If a flow's email shows midnight UTC, wrap the value in convertFromUtc.
If a canvas filter for today returns nothing, use a range from Today() to tomorrow for date and time columns.
If behavior cannot be changed, the column has already been changed once or is a system column. Create a new column and migrate.
seoTitle: Choose the right Dataverse date behavior to avoid off-by-one-day errors
seoDescription: Pick User Local, Date Only or Time-Zone Independent for each date column, and handle the UTC values correctly in canvas apps and flows.
primaryKeyword: Dataverse date only time zone independent

faqs.question: Why is my Dataverse date one day off?
faqs.answer: The column uses User Local behavior, so the stored UTC value shifts across midnight for users in other time zones. Use Date Only behavior for calendar dates.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Date Only and Time-Zone Independent?
faqs.answer: Date Only stores a date with no time. Time-Zone Independent stores a date and time and shows the same clock time to everyone.

faqs.question: Can I change a date column's behavior later?
faqs.answer: A User Local column can be changed once to Date Only or Time-Zone Independent. Existing values are not converted.

title: Model a process with Dataverse Status and Status Reason
shortDescription: Use the built-in Status and Status Reason columns for a row's lifecycle, add your own reasons, restrict allowed transitions and set both from apps and flows.
fullDescription: Every Dataverse table has Status (active or inactive) and Status Reason (the detailed stage). Adding your stages as status reasons gives you views, filters and deactivation behavior for free, and optional transition rules stop rows jumping from New straight to Closed.
problemStatement: A custom Stage choice column duplicates the built-in status, so rows are 'Closed' in one column and still Active in the other, and views show finished work.
whenToUse: Any table with a lifecycle such as new, in progress, closed
When inactive rows should drop out of default views and lookups
When only certain stage changes are allowed
whenNotToUse: Several independent states on one row, which need their own choice columns
Stages that change often per customer, where a lookup to a stage table is more flexible
formulaOrCode:
Columns
  Status          statecode     0 Active, 1 Inactive (fixed for custom tables)
  Status Reason   statuscode    your stages, each belonging to one Status
    Active:    New (1), In Progress (100000001), Waiting (100000002)
    Inactive:  Completed (2), Cancelled (100000003)

Add reasons
  Table > Columns > Status Reason > Edit: pick Active or Inactive in the Status drop-down, then add choices.
  Set the default reason for each status.

Restrict transitions (optional)
  Classic column editor (Switch to classic) > Status Reason > Edit Status Reason Transitions:
  tick "Enable Status Reason Transitions", then for each reason list the reasons it may move to.
    New          > In Progress, Cancelled
    In Progress  > Waiting, Completed, Cancelled
    Waiting      > In Progress, Cancelled
  Any other change is rejected by Dataverse, whichever app or flow attempts it.

Canvas app
  // Set a reason within the same status
  Patch('Service Requests', ThisItem, { 'Status Reason': 'Status Reason (Service Requests)'.'In Progress' })
  // Close: set both columns together
  Patch('Service Requests', ThisItem, {
      Status: 'Status (Service Requests)'.Inactive,
      'Status Reason': 'Status Reason (Service Requests)'.Completed
  })
  // Reopen
  Patch('Service Requests', ThisItem, {
      Status: 'Status (Service Requests)'.Active,
      'Status Reason': 'Status Reason (Service Requests)'.'In Progress'
  })
  // Active rows only
  Filter('Service Requests', Status = 'Status (Service Requests)'.Active)
  // Offer only reasons valid for the row's status is not automatic in canvas: filter the list yourself
  Filter(Choices('Service Requests'.'Status Reason'), Value in [ 'Status Reason (Service Requests)'.'In Progress', 'Status Reason (Service Requests)'.Waiting ])

Power Automate
  Update a row > Status: Inactive > Status Reason: Completed     (set both)
  Filter rows:  statecode eq 0 and statuscode eq 100000001
  Trigger: Select columns: statuscode       Filter rows: statuscode eq 2
  Label:  triggerOutputs()?['body/statuscode@OData.Community.Display.V1.FormattedValue']

Behavior you get for free
  Inactive rows are read-only in model-driven forms, excluded from "Active" views and from lookups by default.
  Deactivate and Activate buttons on the command bar set the default reasons.

Special tables
  Case, Opportunity, Quote and similar have extra states and must be closed with their own actions
  (for example CloseIncident), not a plain update.
stepByStepInstructions: List the stages and decide which are active and which inactive.
Add them as Status Reason values under the right Status.
Set default reasons for Active and Inactive.
Enable transitions if only some stage changes are valid.
Set Status and Status Reason together when closing or reopening rows.
Base default views and app filters on Status = Active.
commonMistakes: Adding a separate Stage column that repeats Status Reason.
Setting a reason that belongs to the other Status without changing Status.
Renumbering or deleting reasons already in use.
Trying to close a Case with a plain update.
troubleshooting: If the update fails with an invalid status code message, the reason does not belong to the status being set.
If a transition is refused, check the Status Reason Transitions list for the current reason.
If closed rows still appear in a gallery, filter on Status = Active.
If reasons differ between environments, the Status Reason column was not included in the solution.
seoTitle: Model a process with Dataverse Status and Status Reason
seoDescription: Use the built-in Status and Status Reason columns for a row's lifecycle, add your own reasons, restrict allowed transitions and set both from apps and flows.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Status and Status Reason in Dataverse?
faqs.answer: Status is Active or Inactive. Status Reason is the detailed stage, and each reason belongs to one status.

faqs.question: How do I deactivate a Dataverse row from Power Apps?
faqs.answer: Patch Status to Inactive together with an inactive Status Reason.

faqs.question: Can I limit which status changes are allowed?
faqs.answer: Yes. Enable Status Reason Transitions on the column and list the allowed next reasons for each reason.

title: Save several Dataverse rows as one transaction in Power Automate
shortDescription: Use Perform a changeset request so a group of Dataverse creates, updates and deletes all succeed or all roll back together.
fullDescription: A flow that creates an order and its lines with separate actions can fail halfway and leave an order with missing lines. The Dataverse connector's changeset scope sends its actions as one transaction. If any action fails, none of them is saved.
problemStatement: A flow fails on the third of five related writes. The first two are already saved, and someone has to clean up half-created data by hand.
whenToUse: Creating a parent with its children
Moving value between rows, where both updates must happen
Any group of writes that makes no sense partly done
whenNotToUse: Long loops with hundreds of rows, which hold locks and can time out
Steps that need a value generated inside the same changeset, which is not available until it completes
formulaOrCode:
Add: Microsoft Dataverse > Perform a changeset request
  It is a scope. Inside it you may add only these Dataverse actions:
    Add a new row | Update a row | Delete a row | Relate rows | Unrelate rows
  They run together as one transaction when the scope completes.

Example: order with two lines
  Compose - OrderId        guid()          generate the ID first so the lines can reference it
  Perform a changeset request
    Add a new row (Orders)
      Order (unique identifier field under advanced):  @{outputs('Compose_-_OrderId')}
      Name:     @{triggerBody()?['orderRef']}
    Add a new row (Order Lines)
      Name:     @{triggerBody()?['lines'][0]?['item']}
      Order:    cnt_orders(@{outputs('Compose_-_OrderId')})
    Add a new row (Order Lines)
      Name:     @{triggerBody()?['lines'][1]?['item']}
      Order:    cnt_orders(@{outputs('Compose_-_OrderId')})

Rules
  Actions inside cannot use each other's outputs (they are sent together). Generate GUIDs up front with guid().
  No Apply to each, Condition or non-Dataverse actions inside the scope.
  Outputs of the inner actions are not available afterwards. Read the rows back if you need generated values.
  If one action fails, the whole changeset fails and nothing is saved.
  Keep it small: tens of operations, not thousands. A changeset runs within the 2-minute transaction limit.

A variable number of rows
  The designer needs fixed actions, so for a dynamic list call the Web API $batch endpoint yourself:
  HTTP with Microsoft Entra ID > Invoke an HTTP request
    POST /api/data/v9.2/$batch
    Content-Type: multipart/mixed;boundary=batch_1
  Body (built with Select + join):
    --batch_1
    Content-Type: multipart/mixed;boundary=changeset_1

    --changeset_1
    Content-Type: application/http
    Content-Transfer-Encoding: binary
    Content-ID: 1

    POST /api/data/v9.2/cnt_orders HTTP/1.1
    Content-Type: application/json

    {"cnt_name":"ORD-1042"}
    --changeset_1
    Content-Type: application/http
    Content-Transfer-Encoding: binary
    Content-ID: 2

    POST /api/data/v9.2/cnt_orderlines HTTP/1.1
    Content-Type: application/json

    {"cnt_name":"Laptop","cnt_Order@odata.bind":"$1"}
    --changeset_1--
    --batch_1--
  "$1" refers to the row created by Content-ID 1, so no pre-generated GUID is needed. Up to 1,000 requests per batch.

Error handling
  Put the changeset in Scope - Try. In Scope - Catch, log the error: nothing needs undoing.
stepByStepInstructions: List the writes that must succeed or fail together.
Generate any IDs the rows share with guid() before the changeset.
Add Perform a changeset request and place the Dataverse write actions inside.
Reference the pre-generated IDs for lookups between the new rows.
Wrap the changeset in a try scope and log failures.
Force a failure in testing and confirm nothing was saved.
commonMistakes: Expecting an action inside the changeset to use another's output.
Placing loops or conditions inside the scope.
Putting hundreds of operations in one changeset.
Assuming non-Dataverse steps, such as sending an email, roll back too.
troubleshooting: If the designer refuses an action inside the scope, only the five Dataverse write actions are allowed.
If lines fail with a missing parent, set the parent's ID explicitly and reference the same GUID.
If the changeset times out, split the work into several smaller transactions.
If you need the autonumber of the new row, get the row by its GUID after the changeset.
seoTitle: Save several Dataverse rows as one transaction in Power Automate
seoDescription: Use Perform a changeset request so a group of Dataverse creates, updates and deletes all succeed or all roll back together.

faqs.question: Can Power Automate roll back Dataverse changes if a step fails?
faqs.answer: Yes, for actions placed inside Perform a changeset request. They are committed together or not at all.

faqs.question: Can I use a loop inside a changeset?
faqs.answer: No. Only Dataverse add, update, delete, relate and unrelate actions are allowed. For a variable number of rows, call the Web API batch endpoint.

faqs.question: How do child rows reference a parent created in the same changeset?
faqs.answer: Generate the parent's GUID beforehand with guid(), set it on the parent and use it in each child's lookup.

title: Read and create Dataverse note attachments in Power Automate
shortDescription: List the notes on a row, get each attachment's content, email or copy the files, and attach a new file as a note from a flow.
fullDescription: Files added through the timeline in a model-driven app are stored as Notes (the annotation table). Each note holds a file name, a type and the content in base64, linked to its parent through the Regarding lookup. Flows can read these to send or archive files, and create them to attach generated documents.
problemStatement: Users attach evidence to a request in the app, and the approval email needs those files, but the flow cannot find them on the request row.
whenToUse: Emailing files attached to a row
Copying attachments to SharePoint for retention
Attaching a generated PDF or received email attachment to a row
whenNotToUse: Very large files in bulk, since content is loaded into flow memory
Tables where attachments are disabled, which need a file column or SharePoint instead
formulaOrCode:
List the notes for a row
  List rows > Table: Notes
    Filter rows:    _objectid_value eq @{triggerOutputs()?['body/cnt_servicerequestid']} and isdocument eq true
    Select columns: annotationid,subject,filename,mimetype,filesize,createdon
    Sort by:        createdon desc
  Do not select documentbody in the list: it is large. Fetch it per note.

Get one attachment's content
  Get a row by ID > Table: Notes > Row ID: items('Apply_to_each')?['annotationid']
    Select columns: filename,mimetype,documentbody
  documentbody is base64 text.

Email all attachments
  Initialize variable varAttachments (Array)
  Apply to each note:
    Get a row by ID (as above)
    Append to array variable:
      {
        "Name": "@{outputs('Get_note')?['body/filename']}",
        "ContentBytes": { "$content-type": "@{outputs('Get_note')?['body/mimetype']}", "$content": "@{outputs('Get_note')?['body/documentbody']}" }
      }
  Send an email (V2) > Attachments: switch to input entire array > @{variables('varAttachments')}

Copy to SharePoint
  Create file > File Name: filename > File Content: base64ToBinary(outputs('Get_note')?['body/documentbody'])

Create a note with a file
  Add a new row > Table: Notes
    Title (subject):                  Signed form
    Description (notetext):           Uploaded by the approval flow
    Is Document:                      Yes
    File Name:                        signed-form.pdf
    Mime Type:                        application/pdf
    Document:                         @{base64(body('Get_file_content'))}        base64 text
    Regarding (Service Requests):     cnt_servicerequests(@{variables('varRequestId')})
  The Regarding field is listed once per table that has notes enabled. Fill the one for your table.
  From an email trigger: Document = items('Apply_to_each')?['contentBytes'] (already base64).

Trigger when a file is attached
  When a row is added > Table: Notes > Filter rows: isdocument eq true and objecttypecode eq 'cnt_servicerequest'
  Parent ID: triggerOutputs()?['body/_objectid_value']

Activities
  Email attachments live in the Attachments (activitymimeattachment) table: filter _objectid_value by the email's ID
  and read body, filename, mimetype.

Size
  Maximum file size is an environment setting (Settings > Email > Maximum file size, default 5 MB, up to about 128 MB).
  Large attachment content may be stored in file storage but is still returned through documentbody.
stepByStepInstructions: Confirm the table has attachments (notes) enabled.
List notes filtered by the row's ID and isdocument.
Get each note's document body in a separate action.
Build an attachment array for email, or create files in SharePoint.
Create notes with Is Document, file name, mime type and base64 content to attach files.
Test with several files and a large file.
commonMistakes: Selecting documentbody in List rows for many notes at once.
Passing binary content where base64 text is expected, or the reverse.
Filtering on the parent's name instead of _objectid_value.
Leaving Is Document off when creating a note with a file.
troubleshooting: If the attachment arrives corrupt, check whether the target wants base64 text or binary and use base64() or base64ToBinary().
If no notes are returned, the files were added to a file column or a SharePoint document location, not as notes.
If the flow runs out of memory or times out, process one note at a time and skip files above a size threshold.
If Regarding cannot be set, enable attachments on the table or pick the correct Regarding field.
seoTitle: Read and create Dataverse note attachments in Power Automate
seoDescription: List the notes on a row, get each attachment's content, email or copy the files, and attach a new file as a note from a flow.

faqs.question: Where are Dataverse attachments stored?
faqs.answer: Files added on the timeline are rows in the Notes table, linked to the parent row by the Regarding lookup, with the content in the documentbody column.

faqs.question: How do I get note attachments in Power Automate?
faqs.answer: List rows from Notes filtered by _objectid_value and isdocument, then get each note by ID and read documentbody.

faqs.question: How do I attach a file to a Dataverse row from a flow?
faqs.answer: Add a new row to Notes with Is Document set to Yes, a file name, a mime type, base64 content and Regarding set to the parent row.

title: Load Excel and SharePoint data into Dataverse with dataflows
shortDescription: Use a Power Query dataflow to import and refresh data in Dataverse tables, with alternate keys for upserts and lookups mapped by business key.
fullDescription: Dataflows bring data into Dataverse with Power Query. They read Excel, SharePoint lists, SQL and many other sources, reshape the data and load it into tables on a schedule. With an alternate key on the target table, each refresh updates existing rows instead of duplicating them.
problemStatement: Reference data is retyped by hand, or a migration flow loops through thousands of rows for hours and fails partway.
whenToUse: One-off migrations from Excel or SharePoint lists
Scheduled refresh of reference data from another system
Loads of thousands to millions of rows
whenNotToUse: Event-driven integration that must happen within seconds, which suits flows
Complex per-row business logic better handled by a plug-in or flow
formulaOrCode:
Create
  make.powerapps.com > Dataflows > New dataflow > Start from blank > name it
  Pick a source: Excel workbook (OneDrive or SharePoint URL), SharePoint Online list, SQL Server, Web API, Text/CSV...
  Transform in Power Query, then Next > Map tables.

Prepare the data in Power Query
  Remove blank rows, trim text, set column types (date, whole number, decimal).
  Text.Trim, Text.Upper for keys.        Table.Distinct on the key column to drop duplicates.
  Choices: map labels to values with a small lookup or a conditional column
    = if [Priority] = "High" then 100000002 else if [Priority] = "Low" then 100000000 else 100000001
  Yes/No: true / false.
  Dates: change type using locale when the file is day-first.

Map tables
  Load settings:  Load to existing table (recommended) | Load to new table | Do not load
  Destination table: Customers
  Select key:  the alternate key (cnt_ExternalId). With a key, refresh upserts: matching rows update, new rows insert.
               Without a key every refresh inserts again.
  "Delete rows that no longer exist in the query output": tick only when the query is the full source of truth.
  Column mapping: auto map, then fix the rest.

Lookups
  The target table's lookup appears as  Account.accountnumber  (table.key column) when the related table has an
  alternate key. Map your source's account code to it. Dataverse resolves the row by key.
  Load order matters: parents first (Accounts), then children (Contacts, Requests). Use separate queries in
  the right order, or separate dataflows refreshed in sequence.

Owner and status
  Map ownerid by systemuser key columns where offered, or set owners afterwards with a flow.
  statecode and statuscode can be mapped with their numeric values.

Refresh
  Refresh manually or automatically (for example daily at 02:00). On-premises sources need a data gateway.
  Dataflow > ... > Show refresh history > download the log for row-level errors.
  Trigger a flow when a refresh completes: Dataflows connector > When a dataflow refresh completes.

ALM
  Create the dataflow inside a solution to move it between environments. Connections are re-created per environment.

Performance and limits
  Standard dataflows load through the Dataverse API: tens of thousands of rows per hour is typical.
  Turn off plug-ins and flows on the target tables during a big migration, or expect them to fire per row.
  For millions of rows, split by date range or use incremental refresh on a modified-date column.
stepByStepInstructions: Create alternate keys on the target tables.
Create a dataflow and connect to the source.
Clean and type the data in Power Query.
Map each query to its table, choose the key and map lookups by key.
Load parent tables before child tables.
Run a refresh, read the refresh history and fix row errors.
Schedule the refresh if the data should stay in step.
commonMistakes: Loading without a key, so each refresh duplicates every row.
Mapping choice labels as text.
Loading children before their parents exist.
Ticking delete-missing-rows on a partial extract.
troubleshooting: If rows fail with a lookup error, the parent's key value is missing or differs by spaces or case.
If dates shift, set the column type with the right locale and check the target column's date behavior.
If refresh is slow, disable real-time flows and plug-ins on the table for the load.
If the key cannot be selected, it is not Active yet or the query has duplicate key values.
seoTitle: Load Excel and SharePoint data into Dataverse with dataflows
seoDescription: Use a Power Query dataflow to import and refresh data in Dataverse tables, with alternate keys for upserts and lookups mapped by business key.

faqs.question: How do I import Excel data into Dataverse?
faqs.answer: Create a dataflow, connect to the workbook, shape the data in Power Query and map it to the table. Choose an alternate key so later refreshes update rows.

faqs.question: Do dataflows update existing rows or create duplicates?
faqs.answer: They update existing rows when you select a key on the destination table. Without a key, every refresh inserts new rows.

faqs.question: How do I map lookup columns in a dataflow?
faqs.answer: Give the related table an alternate key. The lookup then appears as table.keycolumn in the mapping, and you map your source code to it.

title: Get choice labels and lookup names from Dataverse in Power Automate
shortDescription: Read the label of a choice, the name behind a lookup and the formatted text of dates and currency from the OData annotations on every Dataverse row.
fullDescription: A Dataverse row in a flow shows a choice as a number and a lookup as a GUID. The labels are in the same response, as annotations beside each value. Reading them with an expression avoids extra actions and keeps emails and documents readable.
problemStatement: The notification email says 'Priority: 100000002' and 'Customer: 0f8fad5b-d9cb...', so the flow adds a Switch for every choice and a Get a row for every lookup.
whenToUse: Emails, Teams messages and documents built from Dataverse rows
Showing owner, customer or status names
whenNotToUse: Logic that branches on a value, which should compare the number so it survives label changes
Multi-language scenarios needing a specific language, since the label follows the connection user's language
formulaOrCode:
The annotation name
  @OData.Community.Display.V1.FormattedValue          appended to the column's property name

Choice label
  triggerOutputs()?['body/cnt_priority@OData.Community.Display.V1.FormattedValue']                High
  Value: triggerOutputs()?['body/cnt_priority']                                                    100000002

Status and status reason
  triggerOutputs()?['body/statecode@OData.Community.Display.V1.FormattedValue']                   Active
  triggerOutputs()?['body/statuscode@OData.Community.Display.V1.FormattedValue']                  In Progress

Lookup name (note the _value form)
  triggerOutputs()?['body/_cnt_account_value@OData.Community.Display.V1.FormattedValue']          Contoso Ltd
  triggerOutputs()?['body/_ownerid_value@OData.Community.Display.V1.FormattedValue']              Dana Lee
  GUID: triggerOutputs()?['body/_cnt_account_value']
  Which table a polymorphic lookup points at:
  triggerOutputs()?['body/_ownerid_value@Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.lookuplogicalname']               systemuser | team

Yes/No, dates, numbers, currency
  ...['body/cnt_isurgent@OData.Community.Display.V1.FormattedValue']                              Yes
  ...['body/cnt_duedate@OData.Community.Display.V1.FormattedValue']                               09/03/2026 (user format)
  ...['body/cnt_amount@OData.Community.Display.V1.FormattedValue']                                £1,250.00

Multi-select choice
  ...['body/cnt_systems@OData.Community.Display.V1.FormattedValue']                               CRM; Finance
  Values: ...['body/cnt_systems']                                                                 100000000,100000002

Inside a loop over List rows
  items('Apply_to_each')?['cnt_priority@OData.Community.Display.V1.FormattedValue']
In a Select action (Map, text mode)
  item()?['_cnt_account_value@OData.Community.Display.V1.FormattedValue']

From Get a row by ID
  outputs('Get_request')?['body/cnt_priority@OData.Community.Display.V1.FormattedValue']

In the designer
  Dynamic content does not list formatted values for every column. Type the expression in the expression editor.
  Trick: add the plain dynamic value, switch to code view (or peek code) to copy the property name, then append
  the annotation.

If annotations are missing
  They are returned by the Dataverse connector by default. With raw HTTP calls add the header
  Prefer: odata.include-annotations="*"

All labels of a choice (for a mapping table)
  GET /api/data/v9.2/EntityDefinitions(LogicalName='cnt_servicerequest')/Attributes(LogicalName='cnt_priority')
      /Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.PicklistAttributeMetadata?$select=LogicalName&$expand=OptionSet($select=Options)
stepByStepInstructions: Find the column's logical name, and for lookups its _name_value form.
Append @OData.Community.Display.V1.FormattedValue to the property path.
Enter it in the expression editor.
Use the label for display and keep the numeric value for conditions.
Wrap in coalesce() for columns that may be empty.
Remove Switch and Get a row actions that only fetched labels.
commonMistakes: Building a Switch to turn choice numbers into labels.
Branching on labels, which break when someone renames an option.
Forgetting _value when asking for a lookup's formatted value.
Expecting the label in a language other than the connection user's.
troubleshooting: If the expression returns null, check the exact property name in the action's raw outputs.
If a lookup's name is blank, the lookup is empty on that row.
If the label is in the wrong language, change the connection user's Dataverse language or map values yourself.
If an HTTP call returns no annotations, add the Prefer header.
seoTitle: Get choice labels and lookup names from Dataverse in Power Automate
seoDescription: Read the label of a choice, the name behind a lookup and the formatted text of dates and currency from the OData annotations on every Dataverse row.

faqs.question: How do I get the text of a Dataverse choice in Power Automate?
faqs.answer: Use the formatted value annotation: body/columnname@OData.Community.Display.V1.FormattedValue.

faqs.question: How do I get the name of a lookup without another action?
faqs.answer: Read body/_lookupname_value@OData.Community.Display.V1.FormattedValue from the same row.

faqs.question: Should conditions use the label or the value?
faqs.answer: Use the numeric value. Labels can be renamed or translated.

title: Get the current user's Dataverse row, team and business unit in a canvas app
shortDescription: Find the signed-in user's row in the Users table once, then use it to filter 'my' rows, set owners and read their business unit, manager and teams.
fullDescription: User() gives a name and email. Dataverse works with the user's row in the Users table. Looking that row up once at start gives the app a record it can compare with Owner and other user lookups in delegable filters, and a way to read the user's business unit, manager and team memberships.
problemStatement: Filters for 'my requests' compare emails through lookups and show delegation warnings, or the app cannot tell which business unit the user belongs to.
whenToUse: Defaulting owner or requester lookups to the current user
Tailoring the app by business unit, manager or team
whenNotToUse: Security decisions enforced only in the app, which belong in roles and ownership
Guest or external users without a row in the environment's Users table
stepByStepInstructions: Add the Users table as a data source.
Define a named formula that looks up the current user's row.
Filter galleries by comparing owner or user lookups with that record.
Use the record to default lookups on new rows.
Read business unit, manager and teams from the record as needed.
Test with a user whose email differs in case from their sign-in name.
commonMistakes: Comparing Owner.'Primary Email' with User().Email inside Filter.
Looking the user up in every formula instead of once.
Assuming email always matches. Guests and renamed accounts can differ.
Using the result for security instead of roles.
troubleshooting: If nfMe is blank, the user has no enabled row in this environment or the email differs. Use the Entra object ID match.
If the filter shows a delegation warning, compare the lookup with the record, not with text.
If team checks are slow, load nfMyTeams once and test against it locally.
If the Users table is not listed, search for Users in the Dataverse tables list. Its logical name is systemuser.
seoTitle: Get the current user's Dataverse row, team and business unit in a canvas app
seoDescription: Find the signed-in user's row in the Users table once, then use it to filter 'my' rows, set owners and read their business unit, manager and teams.
primaryKeyword: Power Apps current user Dataverse systemuser

faqs.question: How do I get the current user's Dataverse record in Power Apps?
faqs.answer: Look it up in the Users table by email or Entra object ID: LookUp(Users, 'Azure AD Object ID' = GUID(User().EntraObjectId)).

faqs.question: How do I filter Dataverse rows to the current user?
faqs.answer: Compare the owner or user lookup with the current user's record, for example Filter(Table, Owner = nfMe). This delegates.

faqs.question: How do I get the user's business unit?
faqs.answer: Read the Business Unit lookup from the user's row: nfMe.'Business Unit'.Name.

title: Run solution checker as a quality gate before every deployment
shortDescription: Check a solution for performance, security and upgrade problems from the maker portal, the PAC CLI or a pipeline, and fail the release on critical findings.
fullDescription: Solution checker analyses the apps, flows, plug-ins and web resources in a solution against Microsoft's rules. Running it on every export catches formula errors, deprecated APIs and accessibility problems before they reach test. In a pipeline it becomes a gate: critical or high findings stop the deployment.
problemStatement: Problems such as unhandled delegation, deprecated client APIs or missing accessibility labels are found by users in production instead of by a check at build time.
whenToUse: Every release of a solution to test or production
Reviewing a solution received from a partner or another team
Managed Environments that enforce checker results on import
whenNotToUse: Treating a clean report as proof the solution works, since it does not test behavior
Unpacked source folders, as the checker needs a solution zip or an environment
formulaOrCode:
Maker portal
  Solutions > select the solution > Solution checker > Run
  View results > download the report (zip with a .sarif file and an Excel summary)
  Issues tab on the solution shows findings by component with severity and a link to guidance.

PAC CLI
  pac auth create --environment https://contoso-dev.crm.dynamics.com
  pac solution export --name RequestHub --path ./out/RequestHub.zip
  pac solution check --path ./out/RequestHub.zip --outputDirectory ./out/checker --geo Europe
  Options
    --ruleSet "Solution Checker" | "AppSource Certification"
    --ruleLevelOverride ./rule-overrides.json        change or ignore specific rules
    --excludedFiles "*.min.js"
  Output: a results zip containing SARIF, and a summary table of Critical, High, Medium, Low, Informational counts.

Fail a script on findings (PowerShell)
  $out = pac solution check --path ./out/RequestHub.zip --outputDirectory ./out/checker
  $out
  if ($out -match "Critical\s+[1-9]" -or $out -match "High\s+[1-9]") { throw "Solution checker found critical or high issues" }

Azure DevOps (Power Platform Build Tools)
  - task: PowerPlatformToolInstaller@2
  - task: PowerPlatformChecker@2
    inputs:
      authenticationType: PowerPlatformSPN
      PowerPlatformSPN: 'Dev-ServiceConnection'
      FilesToAnalyze: '$(Build.ArtifactStagingDirectory)/RequestHub.zip'
      RuleSet: '0ad12346-e108-40b8-a956-9a8f95ea18c9'
      ErrorLevel: HighIssueCount
      ErrorThreshold: 0

GitHub Actions
  - uses: microsoft/powerplatform-actions/check-solution@v1
    with:
      environment-url: ${{ vars.DEV_URL }}
      app-id: ${{ secrets.CLIENT_ID }}
      client-secret: ${{ secrets.CLIENT_SECRET }}
      tenant-id: ${{ secrets.TENANT_ID }}
      path: out/RequestHub.zip
      error-level: HighIssueCount
      error-threshold: 0

Managed Environments
  Admin centre > Environment > Edit Managed Environments > Solution checker enforcement: None | Warn | Block
  Block rejects imports with critical issues.

Canvas apps
  Solution checker also runs App checker rules (formula errors, accessibility, performance) on canvas apps in
  the solution. Fix those in Studio under the App checker panel.
stepByStepInstructions: Run solution checker from the maker portal and read the report.
Fix critical and high findings, starting with the ones in your own components.
Add pac solution check to your export script.
Fail the script or pipeline when critical or high counts are above zero.
Record any accepted exceptions in a rule override file with a reason.
Turn on checker enforcement for production if you use Managed Environments.
commonMistakes: Running the checker once at the start of a project and never again.
Ignoring medium findings such as accessibility until an audit.
Overriding rules without recording why.
Checking the unmanaged export but deploying a different build.
troubleshooting: If the check fails to start, the geography is wrong or the account lacks access. Set --geo and use an environment admin or service principal.
If findings point at components you did not build, they come from included dependencies. Remove them from the solution or accept with an override.
If the pipeline passes but the import is blocked, the environment enforces a stricter level than your threshold.
If the run is slow, exclude minified third-party script files.
seoTitle: Run solution checker as a quality gate before every deployment
seoDescription: Check a solution for performance, security and upgrade problems from the maker portal, the PAC CLI or a pipeline, and fail the release on critical findings.
primaryKeyword: Power Platform solution checker pac cli

faqs.question: What does Power Platform solution checker do?
faqs.answer: It analyses the components in a solution against a rule set and reports performance, security, reliability, accessibility and upgrade issues by severity.

faqs.question: How do I run solution checker from the command line?
faqs.answer: Export the solution, then run pac solution check --path with the zip file. The results are written as a SARIF file with a severity summary.

faqs.question: Can solution checker block a deployment?
faqs.answer: Yes. Set an error threshold in the pipeline task, or enable solution checker enforcement on a Managed Environment.

title: Put a Power Platform solution under Git source control
shortDescription: Export and unpack a solution into readable files, commit them to Git, and rebuild the managed solution from source for each release.
fullDescription: A solution zip is a binary blob that cannot be reviewed or merged. Unpacking it turns every table, form, flow and app into separate text files. Committed to Git, they give a history of who changed what, pull request reviews and a way to rebuild any past version.
problemStatement: The only copy of the solution is the development environment. Nobody can say what changed between two releases, and a bad change cannot be reverted.
whenToUse: Any solution with more than one maker or more than one release
Teams that need review and traceability
As the base for automated build and deployment
whenNotToUse: One-person prototypes that will be rebuilt
Expecting to edit unpacked files by hand as a normal way of working. Make changes in the environment and export again
formulaOrCode:
One-time set-up
  winget install Microsoft.PowerAppsCLI          (or: dotnet tool install --global Microsoft.PowerApps.CLI.Tool)
  git init RequestHub && cd RequestHub
  pac auth create --name Dev --environment https://contoso-dev.crm.dynamics.com

Option A: clone and sync (simplest)
  pac solution clone --name RequestHub --outputDirectory . --packagetype Both
  # later, after changes in Dev:
  cd RequestHub
  pac solution sync --packagetype Both
  Creates a .cdsproj project with the unpacked files under src/.

Option B: export and unpack
  pac solution export --name RequestHub --path ./out/RequestHub.zip
  pac solution export --name RequestHub --path ./out/RequestHub_managed.zip --managed
  pac solution unpack --zipfile ./out/RequestHub.zip --folder ./src/RequestHub --packagetype Both --allowDelete
  --packagetype Both reads the managed zip next to the unmanaged one so either can be rebuilt.

Canvas apps inside the solution
  pac solution unpack ... --processCanvasApps        unpacks each .msapp into YAML source (preview feature)
  or per app:  pac canvas unpack --msapp ./src/RequestHub/CanvasApps/app.msapp --sources ./src/apps/RequestHub

What you get
  src/RequestHub/
    Other/Solution.xml              name, version, publisher
    Entities/cnt_ServiceRequest/    Entity.xml, FormXml/, SavedQueries/
    Workflows/                      one JSON file per cloud flow
    CanvasApps/                     .msapp files (and source when processed)
    environmentvariabledefinitions/ connectionreferences in Other/Customizations.xml

Commit
  git add -A
  git commit -m "Add approval threshold environment variable and routing flow"
  git push
  .gitignore:  out/   bin/   obj/   *.zip

Rebuild from source
  pac solution pack --zipfile ./out/RequestHub_managed.zip --folder ./src/RequestHub --packagetype Managed
  or with the .cdsproj:   dotnet build --configuration Release      (Release builds managed, Debug unmanaged)

Routine for each change
  1. Make the change in Dev and publish.
  2. pac solution sync (or export + unpack).
  3. git diff: review only what you meant to change.
  4. Commit on a branch, open a pull request.
  5. The build packs the managed zip from the merged source and deploys it.

Native alternative
  Dataverse Git integration (Solutions > Connect to Git, with Azure DevOps repos) commits and pulls from the
  maker portal without the CLI, for environments where it is enabled.
stepByStepInstructions: Install the PAC CLI and create an auth profile for the development environment.
Clone the solution, or export and unpack it, into a Git repository.
Commit the unpacked files with a message that states the change.
After each change in Dev, sync, review the diff and commit.
Build the managed zip from source for deployment.
Protect the main branch with pull request review.
commonMistakes: Committing the zip files instead of unpacked source.
Leaving out --allowDelete, so removed components linger in the folder.
Several makers exporting from one environment and overwriting each other's commits.
Hand-editing XML and never round-tripping through an environment.
troubleshooting: If the diff is full of noise, the export includes version or timestamp changes. Commit after each logical change and keep versions set by the build.
If pack fails with a missing file, the unpack was partial. Unpack again with --allowDelete into a clean folder.
If flows show as one long JSON line, format on commit or accept it. The content still diffs.
If canvas source differs every export, review at screen level and treat the .msapp as the source of truth for now.
seoTitle: Put a Power Platform solution under Git source control
seoDescription: Export and unpack a solution into readable files, commit them to Git, and rebuild the managed solution from source for each release.
primaryKeyword: Power Platform solution source control git

faqs.question: How do I store a Power Platform solution in Git?
faqs.answer: Export the solution, unpack it with pac solution unpack or use pac solution clone, and commit the resulting files.

faqs.question: Should I commit the managed or unmanaged solution?
